entries.title: iOS 27: Release date, Beta, compatible iPhones and all new features
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

Apple has officially unveiled the new features coming to compatible iPhones running iOS 27 later this year, introducing major Apple Intelligence upgrades, changes to Siri, parental controls enhancements and improvements across core iPhone apps.

iOS 27 is currently available as a beta test version for developers and public testers. The software has been going through several months of testing before its full public release – which is likely to happen in the next few weeks. Apple typically launches new versions of iOS in September, often around the second week – making Monday, September 14 a likely release date based on past patterns.

iOS 27 will be supported on every iPhone all the way back to iPhone 11 and iPhone SE 2, though some Apple Intelligence and Siri related features will only be available on newer iPhones.

This hub contains everything Apple has confirmed will be coming in iOS 27 when it launches, including new features, compatible iPhones, beta release information, Apple Intelligence updates and what’s new for Siri.

## What’s New in iOS 27 at a Glance

* **Siri AI**: Apple’s new Siri AI combines personal context, onscreen awareness and web knowledge to deliver more natural conversations, richer answers, app actions and cross-device chat history.
* **Apple Intelligence across apps**: Apple Intelligence expands across Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail, Calendar, Home and Shortcuts, adding smarter suggestions, automation, image generation and context-aware assistance.
* **Smarter Photos editing**: Photos gains Spatial Reframing, Extend and an upgraded Clean Up tool, allowing users to improve composition, expand images and remove distractions more naturally.
* **Child safety and parental controls**: New parental controls include Ask to Browse, Time Allowances, app schedules and enhanced Communication Safety tools designed to give parents more control.
* **Safari and productivity upgrades**: Safari can organise tabs, monitor webpages and build extensions from descriptions, while Passwords, Calendar and Shortcuts gain powerful new AI-powered capabilities.

## iOS 27 release date: When will Apple release iOS 27?

* September 2026

iOS 27 has been in beta since it was unveiled at WWDC in June, but the official version of iOS 27 will not be available to install on compatible iPhones until later in 2026.

Apple has confirmed that the [iPhone launch event](https://www.macworld.com/article/672537/when-is-apples-next-event.html) will take place on September 9, so we anticipate that iOS 27 will be available to download on Monday, September 14, as the iOS download usually closely follows Apple’s September event.

## What is the latest iOS 27 beta?

As of September 1, iOS 27 beta 8 is now available to developers, with the public beta expected shortly.

At this late stage in the development cycle, Apple is focusing on stability rather than adding new features, with recent betas mainly delivering bug fixes, security updates, performance improvements and final polish ahead of launch.

## Siri AI in iOS 27

![Siri AI inside the Dynamic Island in iOS 27](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Siri-AI-iOS-27.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple

By far the biggest upgrade coming in iOS 27 is Siri AI – Apple’s new Apple Intelligence-powered version of Siri. Apple says it is more personal, conversational and capable than the current assistant, with support for natural follow-up questions, personal context, onscreen awareness and up-to-date information from the web.

### Siri AI features

* **More natural conversations**: Siri AI can understand open-ended questions, follow-up requests and more complex natural language, making interactions feel less like issuing simple voice commands.
* **Personal context**: Siri can draw on information stored in Messages, Mail, Photos and Notes to find details and answer questions. For example, you could ask it to find information buried in an old email or message.
* **Onscreen awareness**: Siri can understand what you’re viewing and act on it, such as saving an address from a message, adding an event to Calendar or answering questions about an article.
* **Camera intelligence**: A new Siri Camera mode lets you show Siri something through the iPhone’s camera, then ask questions or perform actions based on what it sees.
* **More capable app actions**: Siri can perform tasks within apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders. It can, for example, edit a recently sent message, add a song to a playlist or handle more complex Apple Music requests.
* **Better general knowledge and web answers**: Siri can use information from the web to answer questions about recent events and tackle more specific or complicated queries than before.
* **Conversation history across devices**: A dedicated Siri app lets users revisit previous conversations, pin important chats and continue conversations across Apple devices using iCloud syncing.
* **More natural Siri voices**: Siri gains more expressive voices, with controls on compatible devices for adjusting speaking pace and expressiveness. Voice customisation requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer.
* **Improved dictation**: Better speech recognition, automatic punctuation, capitalisation and formatting allow users to dictate more naturally when converting speech into text.
* **AI-assisted message replies**: Siri can compose contextual replies in Messages using the conversation, personal information and web searches. Shortcuts can also automate replies to selected contacts, although manual Siri-assisted replies allow users to check and edit the response before it is sent.

For more Siri AI message replies read about [what happened when we made Siri AI Answer all our Messages](https://www.macworld.com/article/3205200/i-made-siri-ai-automatically-answer-all-my-messages-heres-what-happened.html).

### How good is Siri AI?

Siri AI represents a significant improvement over the old Siri, particularly when handling conversational questions, current information and personal context.

Early testing suggests it can deal with far more complicated requests than Siri previously could. Apple Music is a good example: Siri can identify very specific groups of songs, create playlists and combine music knowledge with reasoning.

It could therefore become one of the biggest reasons to upgrade to iOS 27, potentially changing Siri from a basic voice-command system into a more general way of interacting with the iPhone.

However, Siri AI is still in beta. Testing has revealed server failures, incorrect answers, weak reasoning and unexplained limitations, so its usefulness will depend heavily on how much Apple improves reliability before release.

Apple’s approach to AI safety also appears more restrained than some rival chatbots, with Siri designed to avoid excessive flattery, pretending to be human or responding inappropriately to potentially harmful requests.

### When will Siri AI launch?

Apple says iOS 27 arrives in autumn 2026, but Siri AI does not yet have a specific public release date. Apple currently says the new Siri will launch in English later in 2026.

**Regional Siri AI availability**

Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the EU. It will also remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory issues.

### Siri AI compatibility

Some Siri AI features have more demanding hardware requirements than others. In particular, Apple’s new Siri voice customisation controls require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer.

## Apple Intelligence across apps

As well as Siri AI, the enhanced Apple Intelligence will also power new AI-powered features in Apple’s core apps throughout iOS 27. Safari will organise tabs into topics, monitor webpages for changes and even build extensions from natural-language descriptions. Photos is set to gain a new Spatial Reframing edit tools including and an upgraded Clean Up feature. Messages, Mail and Calendar will be able to understand context, suggest actions and create events from simple descriptions.

## New features coming to apps in iOS 27

iOS 27 brings a mix of major Apple Intelligence upgrades and smaller quality-of-life improvements across Safari, Photos, Messages, AirPods, Passwords, Wallet and other core iPhone apps. Apple is also making iOS more adaptable to different screen sizes and orientations, changes that appear to be laying some of the groundwork for its expected folding iPhone.

### Safari

Safari will automatically group tabs into topics, making related pages easier to find. A new Notify Me feature will monitor webpages and alert you to changes such as price drops or products coming back into stock.  
Apple is also adding Describe an Extension, which lets users create custom Safari extensions simply by explaining what they want the extension to do.

![safari notify me logo](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/safari-notify-me-logo.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple

### Photos

Photos gains significantly more powerful [AI editing tools](https://www.macworld.com/article/3194029/i-pushed-ios-27s-ai-photo-editing-tools-to-the-limit.html).

Spatial Reframing/Reframe can alter the composition and perspective of an existing photo, while Extend generates new image content beyond the original frame when straightening a horizon or changing the aspect ratio.

![iOS 27 Image Editing](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/iOS-27-Image-editing.jpg?quality=50&strip=all)

Apple

Clean Up has also been improved, with Fast and High Quality modes for removing unwanted objects. High Quality mode can produce considerably more natural results, although more ambitious edits can still introduce distortions or invented details.

Photos also adds new categories and the [ability to save a frame from a video](https://www.macworld.com/article/3211750/how-to-save-a-video-frame-as-a-high-res-image-in-ios-27.html) as a full-resolution photo. The resulting HEIF or JPG retains the video’s original resolution, date and location metadata rather than simply creating a screenshot.

### Camera

Apple is developing a customizable Camera interface, although it has not appeared consistently throughout the iOS 27 beta cycle. It [could arrive in a later iOS 27 update](https://www.macworld.com/article/3166087/where-are-the-missing-ios-27-features-dont-worry-theyre-still-coming.html).

Apple is also reportedly developing [Apple Reference Image](https://www.macworld.com/article/3210722/what-is-up-with-this-apple-reference-image-rumor.html), an authentication system designed to prove that a photo or video was genuinely captured on an iPhone and has not subsequently been manipulated.

The feature would use additional metadata and Apple’s Private Cloud Compute to authenticate an image and assign it a unique ID. Its usefulness may be greatest for journalists, insurers and investigators rather than as a general solution to AI-generated imagery, particularly because authentication would be optional and social networks frequently remove metadata.

### Messages

![iPhone shortcut to auto reply to messages using AI](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/iPhone-shortcut-to-auto-reply-to-messages-using-AI.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

Messages gets several useful improvements.

You can also [decide what the microphone button beside the text field does](https://www.macworld.com/article/3202129/ios-27-finally-lets-you-hide-the-audio-button-in-messages-heres-how.html). Under Settings > Apps > Messages > Show in Text Field, it can be set to Record Audio, Start Dictation or None. Disabling it does not remove either feature: dictation remains available from the keyboard and audio messages remain in the + menu.

Voice-message playback controls are easier to access, while Apple Intelligence can suggest actions based on a conversation, such as creating a reminder, making a note or finding relevant photos.

Messages will also gain smarter suggested replies that can better reflect the user’s writing style.

### Drawing

![Drawing app how to steps](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/drawing-app-how-to-steps.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

A [new dedicated Drawing app](https://www.macworld.com/article/3215130/ios-27-has-an-intriguing-new-drawing-app-for-scribbling-messages.html) replaces the old hidden handwriting interface. Accessible from the + menu, it uses the familiar pens, colours and drawing controls found in Notes and Markup, with finished drawings sent as images.

### Mail

Mail gains more context-aware smart replies, including responses that can better match the user’s usual writing style.

Apple Intelligence can also surface information from Mail elsewhere in iOS. For example, the Phone app could retrieve a flight confirmation number from an email when you call an airline.

### Phone

A new Call Context feature can surface information that may be useful when calling a business. Apple says the information is selected according to who you are calling rather than by listening to the conversation. For example, calling an airline could cause iOS to surface the relevant flight confirmation from Mail.

Birthday reminders can also appear when calling contacts whose birthdays are stored on the iPhone.

### FaceTime

FaceTime gains Dual Capture, allowing the front and rear cameras to be used at the same time during a call.

### Passwords

![passwords in ios 27 automatically fixing compromised passwords](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/passwords-ios-27-auto-fix.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Passwords in iOS 27 will fix things for you.

Apple

The Passwords app will continue to warn about weak, reused and compromised credentials, but iOS 27 goes a step further by offering to fix some of them automatically.

Using Apple Intelligence, Passwords can visit supported websites, change a vulnerable password and save the replacement credentials. See: [Apple got rid of my biggest password headache](https://www.macworld.com/article/3160935/apple-finally-got-rid-of-my-biggest-password-headache.html).

The usefulness of the feature will depend on how widely websites are supported and how well it handles obstacles such as two-factor authentication and unusual account-management interfaces.

### Shortcuts

Shortcuts gains Describe a Shortcut, allowing users to create automations simply by explaining what they want to happen.

Apple Intelligence will interpret the request and assemble the appropriate actions across supported apps, potentially making Shortcuts significantly easier to use for people unfamiliar with building automations manually.

### Calendar

Calendar can create or modify events from natural-language instructions.

Apple says the app can recognise contacts, locations, dates and other event details as users type, reducing the amount of information that needs to be entered manually.

### Image Playground

Image Playground is becoming considerably more powerful.

Apple says it can create photorealistic images and lets users modify generated pictures simply by describing the changes they want. Individual objects can also be selected, resized or repositioned.

AI-generated images will include a SynthID watermark identifying them as synthetic content.

### Wallet

Wallet can create custom passes from QR codes.

Users can add their own fields and information to the pass, and passes automatically sync to Apple Watch.

### Home app

Apple Intelligence comes to the Home app for compatible HomeKit Secure Video cameras.  
It can group related camera notifications, describe recorded video and highlight clips that appear particularly noteworthy.

### Maps

Apple Maps improves Flyover using higher-quality aerial imagery and Visual Intelligence models.

Apple says this produces sharper architectural detail and more realistic rendering of elements such as individual trees.

### Podcasts

Video podcasts become easier to use, with improved controls for switching between watching a podcast and simply listening to it.

### Fitness

Workout summaries have been redesigned to make them easier to share.

Users can also hide completed Fitness+ workouts.

## iOS 27 changes beyond the iPhone

### CarPlay

CarPlay gains an audio scrubber, giving drivers and passengers more direct control when moving through audio tracks and other content.

### AirPods

iOS 27 introduces several [new AirPods features](https://www.macworld.com/article/3220517/airpods-here-are-the-new-features-in-ios-27.html).

A new Custom EQ lets users independently adjust bass, mids and treble using a simple three-band equalizer under Settings > AirPods > Audio and Routing > Equalizer > Custom.

Compatible AirPods also gain improved Precision Finding through Find My, making individual earbuds easier to locate.

Some features require both iOS 27 and compatible AirPods firmware.

Read [How to tune your AirPods with a custom EQ in iOS 27](https://www.macworld.com/article/3207287/how-to-tune-your-airpods-with-a-custom-eq-in-ios-27.html).

## Other changes coming with iOS 27

It’s not only individual apps that will see changes.

### Home Screen and landscape mode

Apple is making iOS significantly more flexible when dealing with different screen orientations and sizes.  
More Apple apps now work properly in landscape, including Health, Home, Music, Weather and Watch. Dynamic Island and Live Activities can also adapt to landscape orientation. The Home Screen additionally supports extra-large widgets.

These changes could simply improve iPhone usability, but they also appear well suited to Apple’s expected folding iPhone, which is likely to have an unusual, wider aspect ratio.

[Evidence within Apple’s software](https://www.macworld.com/article/3166172/three-ways-the-os-27-betas-give-away-apples-folding-phone-secret.html) also includes new foldState and angleDegrees variables that could allow apps to respond to whether a device is folded and at what angle.

iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has similarly become freely resizable, with Apple apps dynamically rearranging their interfaces as the window changes shape.

### Liquid Glass refinements

![Apple OS](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Apple-OS-27.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple

Apple says Liquid Glass has been refined for better readability, more uniform refraction and improved contrast. A new slider lets users adjust the look from ultraclear to fully tinted, while updated icons, toolbars, sidebars and window shapes add polish.

### Ringtones, alarms and alert volume

iOS 27 finally [separates several sound-volume controls](https://www.macworld.com/article/3219137/finally-ios-27-lets-you-separately-adjust-the-volume-of-ringtones-alarms-and-alerts.html).

Instead of one combined Ringtone and Alerts slider, users can independently adjust:

* Ringtones
* Alarms and timers
* Alerts and system sounds

The change is optional. Under Settings > Sounds & Haptics, turning off Match Ringtone Volume reveals separate controls.

Media and call volume continue to work independently as before.

### Keyboard

iOS 27 introduces a new quick-paste control above the keyboard.

It lets you paste recently copied text, images or screenshots without having to long-press inside a text field, making everyday copy-and-paste considerably faster.

Apple has also made the Liquid Glass keyboard design more consistent across apps.

### Privacy and Find My

iOS 27 introduces the ability to temporarily pause Find My location sharing without notifying the person with whom the location is normally shared.

### Recovery and troubleshooting

Apple is also expanding the iPhone’s recovery interface, giving users more options for diagnosing problems and recovering an iPhone without immediately connecting it to another device.

## System changes and how iOS 27 will make your iPhone faster

Alongside the headline AI features, Apple says iOS 27 includes a wide range of under-the-hood improvements designed to [make iPhones faster](https://www.macworld.com/article/3160623/apple-finally-figured-out-how-to-make-old-iphones-faster.html), smoother and more efficient.

Apple says apps can launch up to 30% faster, newly taken photos can appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% quicker. External drive transfers should also improve, while updates to network performance and the system-wide search index are designed to make connectivity and finding information faster.

The company has also reworked core technologies including CPU scheduling, display performance and processing efficiency. These changes should benefit older iPhones in particular, with Apple promising smoother performance and more efficient battery use on devices as old as the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE.

[Our testing](https://www.macworld.com/article/3185415/ios-27-will-actually-speed-up-your-old-iphone-heres-the-proof.html) of the iOS 27 beta supports those claims. On an iPhone 11 Pro Max, Camera launch time fell from 0.98 seconds in iOS 26 to 0.65 seconds in iOS 27, while Maps improved from 3.01 seconds to 1.36 seconds.  
Everyday use also feels smoother, with more fluid animations, unlocking, Control Center and app transitions. The phone ran cooler during testing too, which could point to improved system efficiency and potentially better battery performance.

More broadly, iOS 27 appears focused on refinement rather than simply adding new features. Apple says it has addressed dozens of common user frustrations, while changes such as more adjustable Liquid Glass effects are intended to improve readability and general usability.

That focus should make iOS 27 particularly worthwhile for owners of older iPhones, even on models that do not support Siri AI. Those devices still gain performance improvements alongside features such as clipboard tools for the keyboard, independent alarm and timer volume controls, custom Wallet passes, Photos changes, larger widgets and Liquid Glass refinements.

## Child safety and parental controls

![Screentime](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screen-time-27.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple

There are lots of improvements coming to parental controls, including new time allowances for entertainments, games, and social media, and new schedule tools for different times of day or days of the week.

This includes new features like an expansion of the existing “ask to buy” feature for apps to websites. Before a child can view a new website, they’ll have to ask for permission.

**Ask to Browse**: Ask to Browse will expand the current Ask to Buy fetaure to the web. Apple says children will need to request permission before visiting new websites, and parents can review requests in Messages before approving.

**Communication Safety**: Communication Safety will continue to help protect children from viewing or sharing nudity in Messages, FaceTime and other apps. Apple says it will also intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos.

**Time Allowances and schedules**: Parents will be able to set Time Allowances across categories such as Entertainment, Games and Social Media. Recommendations are based on a child’s age combined with guidance from clinical and child development experts. Schedules let parents choose which apps are available at different times or on different days.

**Redesigned Screen Time**: Screen Time will get a redesigned interface with an at-a-glance view of average device usage and most-used apps. Apple says parents can quickly limit or extend access in the moment.

**Child accounts and family safety**: Apple says child accounts remain central to age-appropriate protections. Parents can manage app access, web access, communication permissions and Screen Time settings.

Apple says it is working with the American Academy of Pediatrics to adapt its Family Media Plan.

## Accessibility changes coming in iOS 27

Accessibility features will be smarter and more intuitive in iOS 27:

* VoiceOver will get richer image descriptions and better understanding of onscreen content.
* Live Recognition will let users press the Action button to ask questions about their surroundings and receive detailed responses.
* Voice Control will become more intuitive, allowing users to describe onscreen buttons and controls rather than remembering exact labels or numbers.
* Accessibility Reader will be able to handle more complex source material and provide summaries and translation.

## iOS 27 compatibility

![iPhone 11](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/iphone-11.jpg?quality=50&strip=all)

iPhone 11 is supported by iOS 27.

Roman Loyola/IDG

According to Apple, iOS 27 supports iPhones back to the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features require newer hardware.

Support for iOS 27 does not mean every device gets every feature. Apple Intelligence requires an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 or later, while the most advanced on-device AI models require an iPhone 17 Pro or iPhone Air. On iPad, Apple Intelligence requires an M1-class model or the A17 Pro iPad mini, while the newest on-device models require an M4 iPad with at least 12GB of RAM.

There had been speculation that the iPhone 11 series and iPhone SE 2 would miss out on iOS 27 after leaker Instant Digital claimed on Weibo that the 2019 iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max, along with the 2020 iPhone SE 2, would no longer be supported. That prediction proved incorrect, giving those models at least one more year of software support.

However, the iPhone 11 generation is nearing the end of its support life. As we explain in our guide to [how long Apple supports iPhones](https://www.macworld.com/article/675021/how-long-does-apple-support-iphones.html), the iPhone 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max have already been added to Apple’s [Vintage iPhone list](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/102772).

The iOS 27 compatibility list is:

* [iPhone 17e](https://www.macworld.com/article/3097961/iphone-17e-review.html) (launched in **2026**)
* [iPhone 17](https://www.macworld.com/article/2925527/iphone-17-review.html), [17 Pro / 17 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/2921479/iphone-17-pro-max-review.html) (launched in **2025**)
* [iPhone Air](https://www.macworld.com/article/2926985/iphone-air-review-a-whole-lot-less-for-a-whole-lot-more.html) (launched in **2025**)
* [iPhone 16e](https://www.macworld.com/article/2630661/iphone-16e-review.html) (launched in **2025**)
* [iPhone 16 / 16 Plus](https://www.macworld.com/article/2470661/iphone-16-and-16-plus-review.html) and [iPhone 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/2469098/iphone-16-pro-and-iphone-16-pro-max-review.html) (launched in **2024**)
* [iPhone 15](https://www.macworld.com/article/2247687/iphone-15-review.html) / [15 Plus](https://www.macworld.com/article/2104222/iphone-15-plus-review.html) and [iPhone 15 Pro](https://www.macworld.com/article/2091512/iphone-15-pro-review.html) / [15 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/2081235/iphone-15-pro-max-review.html) (launched in **2023**)
* [iPhone 14](https://www.macworld.com/article/1073091/iphone-14-review.html) / [14 Plus](https://www.macworld.com/article/1656045/iphone-14-plus-review-2.html) / [14 Pro](https://www.macworld.com/article/1070324/iphone-14-pro-review.html) / [14 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/1070386/iphone-14-pro-max-review.html) (launched in **2022**)
* [iPhone SE 3](https://www.macworld.com/article/624052/iphone-se-2022-review.html) (launched in **2022**)
* [iPhone 13](https://www.macworld.com/article/544579/iphone-13-review.html) / [13 mini](https://www.macworld.com/article/668144/iphone-13-mini-review-last-of-a-dying-breed.html) / [13 Pro](https://www.macworld.com/article/450981/iphone-13-pro-review.html) / [13 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/538937/iphone-13-pro-max-review.html) (launched in **2021**)
* [iPhone 12](https://www.macworld.com/article/234703/iphone-12-review.html) / [12 mini](https://www.macworld.com/article/234921/iphone-12-mini-review-a-concentration-not-a-reduction.html) / [12 Pro](https://www.macworld.com/article/668053/iphone-12-pro-review.html) / [12 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/668065/iphone-12-pro-max-review-2.html) (launched in **2020**)
* [iPhone SE 2](https://www.macworld.com/article/234116/iphone-se-2020-review-everything-you-need-and-nothing-else.html) (launched in **2020**)
* [iPhone 11](https://www.macworld.com/article/233317/iphone-11-review.html) / [11 Pro](https://www.macworld.com/article/233322/iphone-11-pro-review.html) / [11 Pro Max](https://www.macworld.com/article/668065/iphone-12-pro-max-review-2.html) (launched in **2019**)

The main dividing line for Apple Intelligence remains the iPhone 15 Pro generation: the standard iPhone 15 and all older models can run iOS 27, but they do not support Apple Intelligence.

## FAQ

---

1.

### When is iOS 27 coming out?

Apple hasn’t confirmed exactly when iOS 27 will be available to install, but it usually launches to the general public in September, or at the latest October.

Once iOS 27 launches Apple will likely continue beta development to test new features that weren’t available at launch.

2.

### Should I install the iOS 27 beta?

Installing a beta lets you test new features ahead of release, so you may be keen to install the beta on your iPhone, but before you do beware of the risks.

For most users, the recommendation is simple: don’t install the beta. Pre-release software can be unstable. Bugs, performance issues, and app incompatibility are common as Apple uses the beta period to identify and fix problems before the final version launches.

If, despite our warnings, you’re still eager to try the new features, be sure to make a backup of all important information, passwords, and so on.

If you want to uninstall the iOS 27 beta read: [How to remove an iOS beta from your iPhone.](https://www.macworld.com/article/1067004/how-to-remove-ios-beta-iphone.html)

3.

### Which iPhones get iOS 27?

The iPhone 11 and iPhone SE 2 and newer get iOS 27. However, the new Siri voices feature requires iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro or newer.

entries.title: Apple to Mac developers: It’s time to let go of Intel
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

When Apple introduced its M-series chips, it also marked the beginning of the end for software written for Intel Macs. It’s been nearly six years since then, and Apple has let developers know that they can bring Intel Mac development to a close.

In an email to developers, Apple said:

> We’re reaching out to let you know that universal macOS apps on the Mac App Store that require macOS 13 or later can now remove support for Intel-based Mac computers.
>
> By removing support for Intel-based Mac computers, you can simplify your development and optimize your download and on-device size.

When Apple announced macOS 26 Tahoe last year, the company said it would be the last version to support Intel Macs. This new announcement takes another step toward dropping Intel altogether. A new [Apple support document](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=w5ngl9k2) adds this vital bit of information:

> macOS 27: Final release to support Rosetta — Intel-only apps will no longer run on Mac computers with Apple silicon after this update.

Now it’s up to developers to determine when to stop with Intel code. App designers will need to determine how many of their users still use Intel Macs before they can drop development, which means that some will need to continue to support Intel for a while. If you use an Intel app, reach out to the app developer to find out their plans.

entries.title: GTA 6 on PS5 vs Xbox: Key differences to consider
entries.content:
![Jason and Lucia in a car in GTA 6](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/06tGFhLKvLFIPb9VrneTQiQ/hero-image.jpg)

[*Grand Theft Auto VI*](https://mashable.com/category/grand-theft-auto) launches on Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles. As far as anyone knows, it could be years before there's a PC version of the hotly anticipated open-world crime game (fortunately, [we don't think it will take that long](https://mashable.com/entertainment/gta-6-will-not-launch-on-pc-in-november-explainer)). But if you want to play the game right away, then it's time for you to figure out which version to buy.

After pre-orders opened, IGN reported that PS5 versions of the game were [outselling Xbox at an eight-to-one ratio](https://mashable.com/entertainment/gta-6-preorders-playstation-xbox-outsells). Microsoft denied these numbers, of course, but if IGN's readers are representative of gamers as a whole, then players are certainly leaning in a very clear direction.

So, should you play *GTA 6* on PS5 or Xbox? There are a lot of variables that make this a difficult question to answer. That said, we're going to do our best. Here is everything you need to know before buying *GTA VI* on PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series S/X

SEE ALSO:
[Could GTA 6 teach Gen Z how to be in a relationship?](https://mashable.com/tech/gta-6-relationship-system-gen-z-dating)

## *Grand Theft Auto VI:* PS5 or Series X?

The first thing to note here is that the only *official* gameplay footage we've seen of *GTA 6* comes from a 26-minute [extended look released on Netflix](https://mashable.com/entertainment/gta-6-netflix-extended-look-everything-that-was-revealed) in late August. It [lived up to the hype](https://mashable.com/entertainment/gta-grand-theft-auto-6-extended-look-netflix-fan-reactions), but less than half an hour of carefully curated footage is not a great way to determine the technical ins and outs of a video game.

It's also worth pointing out, though, that the Netflix footage was captured on PlayStation 5. Sony has even said in its marketing that the game "plays best on PS5."

"Thanks to the close partnership between Sony Interactive Entertainment and Rockstar Games, *Grand Theft Auto VI* will play best on PS5 by taking advantage of PS5’s immersive features to deliver a deeply engaging single-player experience when it launches on November 19," a [Sony blog post reads](https://blog.playstation.com/2026/06/24/grand-theft-auto-vi-plays-best-on-ps5-november-19/).

The company hasn't divulged any real details as to how or why it's best on PS5, though. Until the game is in our hands, we can't know for sure, though.

One thing we do know is that *GTA VI* is a graphical powerhouse. [Digital Foundry](https://www.digitalfoundry.net/features/gta-6-an-extended-look-analysis-perhaps-the-most-impressive-showcase-weve-ever-seen-in-real-time-rendering), an outlet known for technical breakdowns of video game visuals, called it arguably "the most impressive example of real-time game rendering" they've seen yet. The power differential between the PS5 and Series X is not particularly significant, so based on what we saw on Netflix, there's every reason to expect that the Xbox Series X version will be comparable, at least.

Just be warned that, according to Digital Foundry (and also according to what little I know about video game rendering), the game will almost certainly not ship with a 60 frames per second mode, and it may not ever get one on these consoles. But 30 FPS is fine; you'll get used to it.

## What about Xbox Series S?

One major question a lot of folks will have is whether *GTA 6* will still look good and play well on an Xbox Series S. Both [Xbox](https://mashable.com/article/microsoft-xbox-announces-console-video-game-price-increases) and [PlayStation](https://mashable.com/article/sony-playstation-ps5-price-hike-economic-pressure) consoles are prohibitively expensive right now due to [RAMageddon](https://mashable.com/tech/ramageddon-every-tech-price-increase-2026), so the cheaper Series S represents the best value of the bunch at $500. It's cheaper because it's a weaker device, though. It's compatible with the same games as the Series X, but [many of those games](https://www.reddit.com/r/XboxSeriesS/comments/17skvn5/what_are_the_worst_series_s_ports_so_far/) are compromised in some way.

We don't know *anything* about the Series S version of *GTA VI* right now. But if I had to guess, I would assume it runs at a lower resolution and has some other settings turned down, at the very least. I would be stunned if Rockstar released it in an unplayable state, but weirder things have happened.

More information about *GTA VI*'s tech specs on these platforms is sure to come out before Nov. 19, and we'll keep you updated as it comes in.

entries.title: What is Boox? Meet the trendy e-readers that BookTok loves.
entries.content:
![A Boox Palma 2 e-reader](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp/hero-image.png)

Just as [BookTok](https://mashable.com/article/booktok-authors-content-creators) goes through phases with its favorite books, it channels the same attitude toward [e-readers](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-e-readers-2026-expert-tested). While [Kindles](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-kindles-2026-expert-tested) are undoubtedly the e-reader to reign supreme, plenty of competitors come in swinging to dethrone it. The latest is Boox.

In between users touting their [Kobo Clara](https://mashable.com/review/kobo-clara-colour-e-reader) and [Kindle Paperwhite](https://mashable.com/review/kindle-paperwhite-12th-gen) on BookTok, you'll also find a passionate, dedicated group of people discussing their Boox e-reader. The Palma Pro 2, in particular, has caught the interest of plenty of folks who want an e-reader even smaller than what Kindle can offer. Having tested several Boox e-readers myself, I was admittedly surprised by the device's popularity because these aren't your regular old e-readers but are instead e-ink tablets.

Unlike Kindles or Kobos, Boox e-readers let you access any app in the Google Play Store, so your books from any app (excluding Apple Books) are all available on one device. Ever dreamed of being able to update your [Storygraph](https://mashable.com/tech/rakuten-kobo-storygraph-integration) or [GoodReads](https://mashable.com/life/most-popular-books-2026-goodreads-members) right on your e-reader? Well, you can download those to your Boox, too.

So here's what to know about Boox, the e-readers that BookTok can't get enough of.

## What is Boox?

![A Boox Palma 2 e-reader](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp/images-1.fill.size_2000x1125.v1788291714.png)

Boox e-readers may be rising in popularity but they've been around for almost two decades.
Credit: Samantha Mangino / Mashable

[Boox e-readers](https://zdcs.link/aXJJve?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Boox%20e-readers&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=aXJJve&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)") are manufactured by Onyx International, a Chinese-based technology company. Onyx created Boox e-readers as an alternative to traditional smartphones and [tablets](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-tablets-2026-expert-tested), which have bright screens that cause eye fatigue and strain. The e-ink tablets have softer interfaces so you can read for hours at a time without bright, glossy blue light.

SEE ALSO:
[How to turn a tablet into an e-reader: The best settings and accessories](https://mashable.com/article/how-to-turn-tablet-into-e-reader)

Onyx e-readers were also among the first to use Android 10, a departure from traditional e-readers like the Amazon Kindle or Rakuten Kobo, which run on independent operating systems.

## Are Boox e-readers or tablets?

But are Boox e-readers actually e-readers? Because Boox runs on an Android operating system, any Android app can be downloaded to the device.

This is very different from Kindle or Kobo, which both run Linux-based operating systems. These unique OSes usually allow you to download and read books and explore new titles. However, there's no option to download other apps and access a home page as you'd expect on a smartphone or tablet.

![A close-up of the Boox Palma 2](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp/images-2.fill.size_2000x1125.v1788291714.png)

Read books on nearly any app on a Boox e-reader.
Credit: Samantha Mangino / Mashable

Boox e-readers do have a library built into their OS, but they also have a standard home screen with access to the Google Play Store. That means any app in the Google Play Store can be downloaded onto the device. Technically, this makes them e-ink tablets, meaning they're like traditional tablets but with a matte e-ink display.

The perk of traditional e-readers is their distraction-free UX, so even though they're still digital devices, they're limited in their capabilities. But a Boox exposes you to more distractions. Luckily, they aren't that powerful and don't have nearly as much computing power as even a smartphone. So even though you have access to a world of apps and the internet, it doesn't mean you have the processing power to fully enjoy them.

## What models of Boox are available?

![Boox Go 6 Gen 2, Go 10.3, and Palma Pro 2 e-readers](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp/images-3.fill.size_2000x1125.v1788291714.png)

There are eight available Boox e-reader and e-ink tablets including the Palma 2 Pro and Go 6 (Gen 2).
Credit: Boox / Mashable

Boox has lots of models, including past generations of current models, but not all of them are available. Here are the current tablets and e-readers available from Boox.

**E-ink tablets**

* [Tab X C](https://zdcs.link/zJ77Bk?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Tab%20X%20C&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=zJ77Bk&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")
* [Note Max](https://zdcs.link/9877w8?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Note%20Max&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=9877w8&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")
* [Note Air5 C](https://zdcs.link/QP44nm?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Note%20Air5%20C&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=QP44nm&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")

**E-readers**

* [Go 10.3 (Gen 2)](https://zdcs.link/aeJJ5X?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Go%2010.3%20%28Gen%202%29&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=aeJJ5X&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")
* [Go 7](https://zdcs.link/aXJJXp?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Go%207&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=aXJJXp&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")
* [Go Color 7 (Gen 2)](https://zdcs.link/QL22gP?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Go%20Color%207%20%28Gen%202%29&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=QL22gP&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")
* [Go 6 (Gen 2)](https://zdcs.link/9yWWVr?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Go%206%20%28Gen%202%29&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=9yWWVr&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")
* [Palma 2 Pro](https://zdcs.link/zn77my?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Palma%202%20Pro&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=zn77my&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")

We're in the midst of testing Boox's e-readers with reviews of the [Go 10.3 (Gen 2)](https://zdcs.link/aeJJ5X?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Go%2010.3%20%28Gen%202%29&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=aeJJ5X&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)") and [Go 6 (Gen 2)](https://zdcs.link/9yWWVr?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Go%206%20%28Gen%202%29&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=9yWWVr&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)") coming soon. For notes on our favorite e-readers, check out our [guide to the best e-readers](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-e-readers-2026-expert-tested).

## Are there privacy and security concerns with Boox e-readers?

When covering Boox's devices, there's some concern about Boox's privacy and security. This stems from Boox e-readers being designed and manufactured in China, and some users are concerned that the devices "phone home," meaning they send data back to servers in China. To be fair, on a Kindle, Amazon also takes your data, following nearly every book you read, including your bookmarks and annotations.

There are no known security threats associated with using a Boox e-reader; however, if you'd prefer to be in control of your data, you can download an app like NetGuard to your Boox e-reader via the Google Play Store. [NetGuard](https://zdcs.link/akjjAw?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=NetGuard&object_type=article&object_uuid=04cQtiFTQFPk0A7kAbBWztp&short_url=akjjAw&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)") is a cybersecurity app that lets you block WiFi usage for certain apps, allowing only the apps you want to operate over your network. Since Kindle runs on a closed system, you can't install NetGuard on your device. If you want more control over your data, a Boox e-reader might be a better option.

entries.title: Uber Is Laying Off 10% of Its Workforce
entries.content:
Uber is laying off about 3,300 employees, or roughly 10% of its workforce, as part of a restructuring aimed at cutting management layers and redirecting investment toward ridesharing, delivery, and robotaxis. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi announced the changes in an internal email that was also published online.TechCrunch reports: According to the email, the layoffs are part of a restructuring exercise that would shrink the number of managers by 20%, and some personnel in these roles would work as individual contributors going forward.
The ridesharing giant is reducing the number of teams with one or two members by 50%, and letting go staff who are "more than seven layers down from the CEO," per Bloomberg. Khosrowshahi's email said the company is combining its engineering, science, and delivery divisions. The company is also bringing together its delivery operations across restaurants, retail, and direct divisions.
Remote jobs at the company are going away, too, with Uber only allowing less than 1% of its staff to work remotely.

[![](https://a.fsdn.com/sd/twitter_icon_large.png)](http://twitter.com/home?status=Uber+Is+Laying+Off+10%25+of+Its+Workforce%3A+https%3A%2F%2Ftech.slashdot.org%2Fstory%2F26%2F09%2F02%2F161253%2F%3Futm_source%3Dtwitter%26utm_medium%3Dtwitter)
[![](https://a.fsdn.com/sd/facebook_icon_large.png)](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Ftech.slashdot.org%2Fstory%2F26%2F09%2F02%2F161253%2Fuber-is-laying-off-10-of-its-workforce%3Futm_source%3Dslashdot%26utm_medium%3Dfacebook)

entries.title: Google ships its third Gemini Flash model in six weeks
entries.content:
Google hasn’t released a Gemini Pro model in a while, but on Wednesday, the company [launched](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/3-8-flash-and-3-8-flash-cyber/) yet another set of Gemini Flash and Flash Cyber models.

Even though Gemini 3.7 Flash is only three weeks old (and this is Google’s third Flash release in six weeks), the new Flash model often outperforms it by quite a margin, especially on agentic coding tasks and agentic computer use.

Like before, Flash 3.8 will be available at $0.75/$3.75 per million input/output tokens. That’s the introductory price, though. It will expire on December 31, 2026, and go to $1.50/$7.50 then.

## Fairwind gates Flash 3.8 Cyber

Flash 3.8 looks to be a very good model, and Google is right in calling it its “workhorse model,” but Flash 3.8 Cyber is worth a mention, too. With this, Google is essentially copying the Anthropic playbook.

Google describes the Cyber model as its “most capable cybersecurity model with frontier-level performance in vulnerability detection and automated patching.” And because of this, it’s only available to a select number of “trusted defenders” through a new program Google calls [Fairwind](https://deepmind.google/fairwind-program/).

These include about 650 trusted partners like Accenture, CrowdStrike, the Center for Internet Security, Datadog, Palo Alto Networks, Snowflake, and Wiz.

“The defender’s edge comes from shrinking the time between detecting a flaw and patching it,” Four Flynn, Google’s VP for Security and Privacy, writes in the [announcement](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/safety-security/fairwind-program/). “Through Google’s Fairwind Program, government and enterprise partners gain autonomous tools to repair systems faster and at scale, keeping them one step ahead of agentic-speed threats.”

With Flash 3.5 Cyber, Google had launched a limited-access program, but that didn’t have a name and seemed a bit ad hoc at the time.

## Gemini 3.8 Flash: long-horizon coding and agents

As for Flash 3.8, Google notes that the new model often outperforms models like GPT-5.6 Sol from OpenAI and Claude Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 from Anthropic when it comes to working on complex engineering tasks. On benchmarks like DeepSWE, for example, it matches Opus 5 and beats GPT-5.6 Sol and Sonnet 5.

There’s a caveat here, though, in that Google also stresses that “3.8 Flash works harder.” But working harder means it will also use more tokens, and Google, to its credit, is open about that and notes that, “On complex tasks, it exhibits greater diligence — executing extra reasoning steps, and calling tools iteratively. At times, the model might use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher effort levels.”

To counteract this, developers can choose between different reasoning modes, though, just like with previous models.

![](https://cdn.thenewstack.io/media/2026/09/ce2cb6f2-hromzf5boaalg1y-836x1024.png)

Credit: Google.

Google’s benchmarks do not include [Anthropic’s Fable 5.1](https://thenewstack.io/anthropic-fable-5-1-launch/), which was only released a day earlier. That’s a much stronger model, but also far more expensive.

Nobody would call Fable 5.1 a workhorse model, but it’s worth highlighting that on general agentic benchmarks like Terminal-Bench 4.0, where Flash 3.8 scores 19.1%, Fable 5.1 hits 55.8%, and Opus 5 gets to 51.8%. Meanwhile, on Terminal-Bench 2.1, which focuses on coding, Flash 3.8 does better than its competitors.

Terminal-Bench is the outlier here, though, as the Gemini model actually does quite well on other agentic tasks, even when compared to other flagship models.

Where Google’s model still struggles, despite some impressive gains, is on computer use (59% vs. 75.4% on OSWorld-2.0 for Opus 5) and GDPVal, a benchmark that tests models on knowledge work tasks, where Google, at 1545, remains well behind Opus 5 at 1824 but is finally catching up to Sonnet 5 at 1584.

Google notes that it was able to improve the model in such a short time in part because it’s now using agentic loops to improve the models, too. “Both of today’s releases are powered by the same foundational intelligence, and further accelerated by long-running agentic loops designed to recursively evaluate and refine the underlying models,” the team writes.

## Chinese models close the gap

One thing worth noting is that Google’s comparison focuses on OpenAI and Anthropic, but it’s hard not to notice that on some benchmarks like DeepSWE 1.1, some of the Chinese models like GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3 Flash, as well as DeepSeek v4 Pro and Kimi K3, are very much in the same league, too — and they often offer even better price/performance ratios.

![](https://cdn.thenewstack.io/media/2026/09/8b98daca-gemini-3-8-flash__evals__deepswe.width-2000.format-webp-1024x576.webp)

Credit: Google.

## Cyber benchmarks

As for Flash 3.8 Cyber, Google says it delivers “frontier-level performance in autonomous vulnerability discovery” on CyberGym, where it beats 3.5 Flash Cyber, which was released in July, and “significantly larger frontier models.”

CyberGym only covers C and C++ code, so Google also tested the model on an internal benchmark that spans 20 languages and reports a success rate above 70% there.

On Collinear’s CWE-Bench, the model scores a pass@1 of 47.2%, just behind “a leading frontier model at 47.8%” that Google doesn’t name.

Benchmarks only go so far, though. Chrome’s security team says the model produced 2.6 times more correct patches than “the best commercial models that are much larger,” while Wiz reports 7.5% to 9.7% higher recall on its internal penetration testing benchmark at 2.3 to 5.2 times lower cost.

## Safety

On the safety front, Google says that 3.8 Flash is shipping “with safeguards against misuse in the domains of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) and cyber offense, while enabling beneficial use cases, as per our [Frontier Safety Framework](https://deepmind.google/blog/strengthening-our-frontier-safety-framework/).”

Gemini Flash 3.8 Cyber has a more permissive set of safeguards, but that’s why it is only available to a select group of users, too.

Google does note that the new model is far more robust when it comes to prompt injections, too, with (almost) class-leading results in the Gray Swan IPI benchmark, for example.

![](https://cdn.thenewstack.io/media/2026/09/cce3a0e3-gemini-3.8-flash_evals_attack__l.width-2000.format-webp-1024x576.webp)

## Gemini Pro?

The release of the next Gemini Pro model will be interesting. These Flash models are improving rapidly, and while Google has fumbled the Pro launch a bit, that model may have been worth the wait. Google’s strategy to bet on its Flash models in the meantime also means that it has been able to push a price/performance narrative that has been harder to tell for other U.S.-based frontier labs.

At this rate, though, we may see a Gemini 3.9 Flash before Gemini 4 Pro arrives.

## Availability

Gemini 3.8 Flash is now available in the usual Google products like Antigravity, Google AI Studio, Android Studio, and Stitch, as well as Gemini Enterprise.

Consumers with AI Pro and Ultra subscriptions can also use it in the Gemini App, AI Mode in Google Search, and Gemini in Google Sheets.

The post [Google ships its third Gemini Flash model in six weeks](https://thenewstack.io/google-ships-its-third-gemini-flash-model-in-six-weeks/) appeared first on [The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io).

## 应用介绍

**功能概述**：  
***目录***  
任何硬盘，数据文件夹，CD -ROM ， DVD-ROM ， blueray， HD-DVD ， iPod，服务器卷，音频光盘， U盘， FTP服务器，和更多设备

真的处理大量数据

创建美丽的缩略图许多照片和图像格式，如JPG ， TIFF，EPS ， RAW ， PDF ， PSD ， BMP，GIF ， PNG，TGA ， IFF （玛雅）

支持MP3，AAC （ iTunes的） ， FLAC （无损） ， ALAC （苹果无损） ，和AIFF元数据：作者，专辑，标题，作曲家，歌词，封面，曲目编号，时间，比特率，类型，今年，注释。甚至整个编目音频CD和苹果iPhone铃声文件

拿到维度，时间，编解码器和帧速率出来的电影文件，支持AVI，MOV ， MP4，FLV ， MPG ， M4V

分享你的整个工作组的CDFinder数据库（需要营业执照）

***跨平台***  
使用CDWinder （ CDFinder适用于Windows） ，您可以使用一个数据库两全其美！

***工作流程整合***  
自动编目由Roxio的吐司烧毁所有碟片，直接从CDFinder任意拖动图像到像Adobe公司的InDesign ， Quark Xpress等，苹果网页， Microsoft Office应用程序;整合CDFinder到的FileMaker Pro数据库，以及更多

***输入组织***  
这十二格式支持：磁盘召回， DiskWizard ，艾美加FINDIT ，预兆DiskTracker （ ！既1.x和2.x ） ，目录， CatFinder ， “ Neometric ”目录， DiskLibrary ，残破的十字架磁盘管理器（ Windows）中，和高级磁盘目录（ADC适用于Windows）目录或导出文件，以及iView中MEDIAPRO和Microsoft Expression Media中的XML文件（需要单独CDFinder运输车（ iView中） ）;  
快速，好不好用，见截图  
导出和打印目录数据，并打印CD或DVD封面。嵌卡，和小册子

***预览***  
看里面的存档文件：ZIP ， TAR ， RAR ，StuffIt ，和其他人，包括磁盘映像的内容。 （seat，甚至sitx 。 ）
