🌟 精彩内容

💡 AGI 不会只在实验室里被“发明”

Koray 对 AGI 的理解不是某个研究团队闭门攻关后突然交付的终点，而是模型、产品和用户共同参与的持续建设过程。产品越接近真实需求，模型获得的反馈信号就越丰富，研究方向也越清晰。

“我们就是要通过产品来构建智能。”

💡 benchmark 是地图，但不是全部的进步

Benchmark 能够把能力量化，也能帮助研究团队明确下一座“山”在哪里；但当模型接近或突破某个测试后，它就可能不再代表新的 frontier。真正重要的进步，还要看模型是否进入现实世界，并为不同职业、不同语言和不同任务提供更大价值。

“衡量进步最重要的标准，就是我们的模型进入现实世界，科学家用它们，学生用它们，律师用它们，工程师也用它们。”

💡 Vibe Coding 让更多人成为建设者

代码不再只是软件工程师的专属工具。借助自然语言和模型能力，拥有创意的人可以直接把想法变成可运行的应用，从“有想法”走向“能生产”。这意味着 AI 的影响不只是提高专业人士的效率，也可能扩大能够创造数字产品的人群。

“突然之间，你就让更多人成了构建者，开始做东西。”

💡 用户反馈是模型训练的一部分

Antigravity、AI Studio、Gemini app 和 Search AI Mode 不只是模型的展示渠道，也成为模型团队观察真实使用、发现缺陷和判断优先级的关键入口。模型只有与用户和产品紧密连接，才能知道哪些能力在现实里真正重要。

“直接了解用户非常重要。”

💡 Gemini 不是一种固定架构，而是一个持续追求的目标

Koray 不把 Gemini 等同于某一种永远不变的模型架构。Pro、Flash、Flash-Lite，以及未来可能出现的不同模型，都只是围绕速度、成本、准确率和能力取舍的具体实现。Gemini 真正要实现的是“智能”，以及让这种智能通过产品服务于全世界。

“Gemini 不是那个架构，Gemini 是你想要实现的目标。”

💡 Gemini 最大的风险不是规模不够，而是失去创新

即使模型已经在多个 benchmark 上达到领先，也不能因此认为已经找到了可以机械复制的配方。继续扩展规模固然重要，但新的架构、新的训练方法、新的研究方向和新的产品反馈同样不可缺少。

“Gemini 最大的风险，就是失去创新。”

💡 安全不是发布前最后加上的一层包装

在 Koray 看来，安全与安保必须从数据、pre-training、post-training 和发布候选版本开始，就成为模型工程流程中的核心指标。它应当像 GPQA、HLE 等能力 benchmark 一样，被持续测量、持续迭代，而不是产品完成后才补上的功能。

“我们会再次从工程思维出发，从底层、从一开始就考虑这些问题，而不是等到最后才加上去。”

💡 追赶者也可以把规模变成优势

Koray 坦诚讲述了 Gemini 从并非所有方向都领先，到逐渐进入 frontier 行列的过程。追赶并不只是模仿别人，还意味着学习已有方法、承认自己的不足，并在技术、流程、模型和组织方式上形成独有的解决方案。

“你得对自己诚实……不过，你得为自己做创新。”

entries.title: NASA scientists discover a giant 10-sided pattern on Saturn
entries.content: A huge 10-sided atmospheric pattern has appeared around Saturn’s south pole, giving the planet a surprising counterpart to its famous northern hexagon. Hubble data suggest the strange decagon only began emerging in the past few years and is still growing stronger. Researchers hope continued observations will reveal why it suddenly formed and whether it could persist for decades.
entries.summary: 哈勃望远镜数据揭示土星南极出现新的十边形大气图案，目前仍在持续增强。

entries.title: Ancient “living fossils” may reveal how complex life began
entries.content: A newly discovered microbe living inside ancient stromatolite communities may offer a rare look at how complex life first emerged. Researchers captured the first direct images of an Asgard archaeon physically connected to a bacterium, with the two microbes appearing to exchange nutrients and other compounds. Scientists think similar partnerships billions of years ago may have helped produce the first complex cells.

entries.title: Quantum control algorithm looks to explain how birds migrate
entries.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
entries.content: The hidden world of quantum mechanics exists at scales many orders of magnitude smaller than living organisms, yet scientists have long theorized that quantum effects play an important role in biology. Birds' ability to sense magnetic fields during migration is one of the best-known mysteries in this field, with leading theories suggesting that this sensing could be achieved by exploiting quantum entanglement.

entries.title: Farewell black spruce? How climate change and pests are reshaping North America's forests
entries.source: Phys.org - latest science and technology news stories
entries.content: More than 80% of North American forests could face greater threats from pests and diseases by midcentury, a University of British Columbia-led study finds. If global emissions continue unchecked, rising temperatures and shifting rainfall patterns could amplify tree pests and diseases across more than 80% of North American forests within decades, jeopardizing critical carbon sinks, air quality and the forestry economy.

entries.title: 16 glistening galaxies shine in new images form NASA’s Chandra X-Ray Observatory
entries.content:
While we have months to wait for the first images from the [freshly-launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope](https://www.popsci.com/science/nancy-grace-roman-space-telescope-launch/), NASA’s other incredible observatories do not disappoint. The agency released a [new collection](https://science.nasa.gov/gallery/galaxy-gallery-galactic-gems-glisten-in-new-gallery-from-nasas-chandra/) of 16 galactic images taken with the [Chandra X-ray Observatory](https://www.popsci.com/science/nasa-chandra-back-catalog/) and other telescopes.

Galaxies are separated into three main categories—[spirals](https://www.popsci.com/science/jwst-whirlpool-galaxy/), [ellipticals](https://www.popsci.com/science/spiral-galaxies-v-elliptical-galaxies/), and [irregulars](https://www.popsci.com/science/early-galaxy-cosmic-grapes/). Spirals are like our own Milky Way and appear to spin around a central focus. Ellipticals are older galaxies and likely the results of mergers. Irregulars that can encompass a wide range of galactic phenomena.

Spirals, ellipticals, and irregulars are all represented in this new collection. Each image hasX-ray data from Chandra, combined with data from other telescopes such as the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Hubble, IXPE, Swift, and NuSTAR, and others both in space and on the ground. Gaze into the galaxies in the gallery below. *(Click to expand images to full screen.)*

## NGC 16-72

![A barred spiral galaxy featuring a prominent central bar or bridge of stars that channels gas toward its core. Chandra X-rays (purple) highlight growing black holes along the bar and core, merged with Hubble optical light (white, yellow and soft blue) and JWST infrared dust filaments (red). Studying barred spirals in action can help reveal how gas in our own Milky Way, which is also a barred spiral, feeds its central black hole and forms new stars. Image X-ray: NASA/CXC/SAO; Optical: NASA/ESA/STScI/Hubble Heritage Team; Infrared: NASA/ESA/CSA/STScI/J. Lee and T. Williams; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/L. Frattare, J. Major, K. Arcand.](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/NGC-1672.png?strip=all&quality=85)

A barred spiral galaxy featuring a prominent central bar or bridge of stars that channels gas toward its core. Chandra X-rays (purple) highlight growing black holes along the bar and core, merged with Hubble optical light (white, yellow and soft blue) and JWST infrared dust filaments (red). Studying barred spirals in action can help reveal how gas in our own Milky Way, which is also a barred spiral, feeds its central black hole and forms new stars. *Image X-ray: NASA/CXC/SAO; Optical: NASA/ESA/STScI/Hubble Heritage Team; Infrared: NASA/ESA/CSA/STScI/J. Lee and T. Williams; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/L. Frattare, J. Major, K. Arcand.*

## II Zw 096

![A chaotic, dust-shrouded system of merging galaxies forming stars at a furious rate. Chandra X-ray data (magenta) pinpoint powerful black hole activity and hot gas, while Hubble optical (blue and white) and Webb infrared (red and grey) data illuminate vast stellar nurseries hidden behind interstellar dust. Systems like II Zw 096 show us how powerful galaxy collisions shaped the early universe. Image: X-ray: NASA/CXC/SAO; Optical: NASA/ESA/STScI; Infrared: NASA/ESA/CSA/STScI; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/L. Frattare and J. Major.](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/iizw096.png?strip=all&quality=85)

Frattare and J. Major.*

## M33

![A nearby, face-on spiral galaxy whose clear spiral arms offer an unhindered view of its stellar engine. X-ray data from Chandra (purple) highlights point sources like neutron stars and stellar-mass black holes pulling material off companion stars (systems called X-ray binaries), while optical data from the Very Large Telescope’s MUSE instrument (pink and grey) maps glowing pockets of hydrogen gas. Ultraviolet data from NASA’s Swift telescope (blue) reveals populations of young, massive stars sizzling across the spiral arms. M33’s proximity to us allows astronomers to audit individual high-energy objects and map how stellar feedback affects a galaxy's ecosystem. Image: X-ray: NASA/CXC/SAO; Optical: ESO/VLT; UV: NASA/Swift; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/L. Frattare.](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/m33.png?strip=all&quality=85)

Chandra's X-rays (royal blue) show superheated shockwaves created by central black hole jets, combined with optical light from Hubble (red, yellow and pale blue) and infrared dust filaments from Webb (bright orange). entries.title: Explore what Pompeii looked like before catastrophic eruption
entries.content:
A little less than 2,000 years ago, Mount Vesuvius became the antihero of the ancient world’s most well-known tragedy. The infamous explosion covered Pompeii and Herculaneum in volcanic debris, immortalizing the final moments of the ancient Roman cities and some of their unfortunate inhabitants in stunning detail.

Now, however, visitors can witness the glory of Pompeii before it all came crashing down in 79 CE. A former game engineer from Illinois and his team have developed an application that brings sites at the Archaeological Park of Pompeii to unprecedented life via Immersive Extended Reality technology. In other words, you can now stand in the forum alongside other ancient Romans and watch in horror as Mount Vesuvius starts to rumble along the horizon.

Todd Porter, the former game engineer and now founder of the software company Histoury, went through a different kind of horror to make it happen—walking every inch of the archaeological sites to execute 155 scans under southern Italy’s blazing sun.

## An idea ahead of its time

Porter founded Histoury less than three years ago, but the lightning bolt of inspiration originally struck him 15 years ago on a visit to Herculaneum, Porter tells *Popular Science*. It was while wandering around the archaeological sites that he had the idea of using his video game background to reconstruct his surroundings in a virtual world one could visit with their phones.

Of course, in 2012, smart phones didn’t have enough processing power to support the sort of software required for something like that. “It only took 13 years for phones to catch up to my vision,” Porter jokes.

But that vision could only manifest with the Pompeii archaeological park’s consent. Thankfully, a member of the team—a former hotel front desk employee who, after learning about the team’s project, offered to quit his job and do their business development—wouldn’t take no for an answer. He knocked on Pompeii’s door every day until, possibly out of exhaustion, the park agreed to a demonstration.

**[ Related: [DNA reveals new stories about Pompeii’s victims](https://www.popsci.com/science/pompeii-dna/) ]**

## The scanner looks like a bomb

Histoury’s digital reconstructions start with two different kinds of scans—a high resolution scan and a spatial scan.

The high resolution scan creates a virtual 3D model of the site with an accuracy range of less than 2 centimeters, and involves walking around the archaeological site with an instrument called a LiDAR scanner.

“That’s just me walking around with a device that looks like a bomb,” Porter says. “It’s shaped like a giant pill with a light whirling around and it makes a noise. You hold it with one hand and you’re looking at your phone with the other.”

![An older white man with white hair and black sunglasses sits holding what looks like a black microphone. ](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Histoury-scanner.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

Todd Porter, the former game engineer and now founder of the software company Histoury, walked around with this scanner capturing every inch of Pompeii. *Image: Histoury, Inc.*

The resulting 3D model is then converted into 3D mesh—essentially a kind of digital model compatible with the game development software they use. Histoury’s artists then build the reconstruction directly on top of this 3D mesh, in consultation with a team of archaeologists to make sure everything is as historically accurate as possible.

The other scan—the spatial scan—employs a less powerful instrument called an Xgrid Portalcam, and serves several different purposes. The main one is to secure spatial accuracy. Traditional GPS data is largely inaccurate. Instead, Histoury’s application uses artificial intelligence to determine where the user is standing and which way they are facing within six inches of accuracy. The AI matches the image captured by the smart phone to images of known locations in its data.

The other purpose of the spatial scan is to allow artists to double check their work without having to visit Pompeii in person. “We blend the two [scans] in our tool set so that the artist can walk around and they can switch back and forth between their recreation and the real world just to triple check that everything is lined up,” Porter explains. “AI is really sloppy with a lot of things. Music, art, but the stuff that it’s really good at is the stuff we use it for, which is number crunching.”

In the final step, the team’s lead AI expert has AI agents that “walk” the entire digital reconstruction, looking in every direction. Simply put, these walk-throughs help check how accurate the spatial aspect of the reconstruction is.

“If it’s not accurate at all or less than a certain percentage, it sends the team back to the site for another spatial scan,” Porter explains. “It means we don’t have to send people on site to stand in 5,000 different places to figure out our accuracy,” says Porter. “We can do that virtually.”

**[ Related: [What did Pompeii smell like before it burned?](https://www.popsci.com/science/what-pompeii-smell-like-before-burn/) ]**

## A magical project

The final product is a smart phone or tablet application, Portyl, that shows what Pompeii would have looked like before Mount Vesuvius’ devastating explosion wherever you point your device. The recreation is populated with people, animals, sound effects, and audio explanations. It’s about as close as you can get to strolling through Pompeii before it was demolished.

The reconstructed sites available for virtual tour currently include Pompeii’s amphitheater, large theater, small theater, [quadriporticus](https://penelope.uchicago.edu/encyclopaedia_romana/gladiators/quad.html) (a space turned into a gladiator training school), [House of the Citharist](https://www.pompeiscavi.com/en/map/regio-1-eng/) (a large aristocratic house), forum, and basilica. The team is also working on additional Pompeii locations. Everything is free until September 1, and the app is accessible even for people who aren’t there in person.

![Digital rendering of a large Roman amphitheater.](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Screenshot-2026-08-17-at-9.56.31-AM.png?strip=all&quality=85)

The amphitheater of Pompeii is one of the oldest Roman amphitheaters in the world. When you download Histoury, you can see what this massive theater would’ve looked like in its prime. *Image: Histoury, Inc.*

But for those who are in Pompeii, “you hold your phone or iPad up, we recognize where you’re standing usually within six inches and we know exactly where you’re facing and then we basically spawn the recreation right there,” Porter says enthusiastically.

“Like in the amphitheater, you’re walking around gladiators fighting. There’s 30,000 people in the crowd around you, and you hear the roar, and you hear the clang of the metal. Of all the things I’ve ever done in my life, this is truly one of the most magical things I’ve ever been part of. I think that’s what really gets everybody—it gets you emotionally.”

Histoury is close to signing a contract with Herculaneum and making moves in other countries, including Egypt.

## The complexities of AI in Pompeii

This isn’t the first time AI has been put to work at Pompeii. Earlier this year, the archaeological park [released an AI-generated video based on archaeological data](https://www.facebook.com/reel/2522475971520533) depicting the final moments of a man whose skeleton was discovered outside of one of Pompeii’s gates. In our article on the subject, [we paused to wonder what the victim would have thought](https://www.popsci.com/science/ai-pompeii-victim-with-mortar-recreation/) about people watching his terrified face to the sound of “Dark Horror Intro” royalty free music.

Since Histoury’s Portyl users can trigger the explosion of Mount Vesuvius and then watch it erupt to the sound of screams and the sight of people running for their lives, the question perhaps stands in this case, too.

**[ Related: [AI makes Pompeii victim’s final moments look shockingly real](https://www.popsci.com/science/ai-pompeii-victim-with-mortar-recreation/) ]**

But they can also simply peer around the basilica or the amphitheater, and there’s something uniquely respectful about paying tribute to Pompeii’s former glory instead of adoring its tragic remains. And more broadly, there’s no denying the fact that a live reconstruction has the potential to make ancient history feel closer than it has ever been before, especially for people who have a hard time imagining the bygone world on their own.

Virgil once wrote, “[fugit irreparabile tempus](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.abe0953),” meaning “irretrievable time flies.” The ancient poet may have thus been surprised to learn that today, time is indeed retrievable—at least somewhat.

The post [Explore what Pompeii looked like before catastrophic eruption](https://www.popsci.com/science/pompeii-reconstruction-app/) appeared first on [Popular Science](https://www.popsci.com).

entries.title: iPhone 18 Pro chip leak hints at performance upgrades in two key areas
entries.content:
A supply chain leak has provided new information on the A20 Pro chip that's set to power the upcoming [iPhone 18](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone-18 "iPhone 18") Pro, detailing how improved gaming performance and more fluid everyday use are in the cards.  
  

![Row of five modern iPhones in different colors, showing rear triple cameras and one front display, arranged from dark gray to white, light blue, pink, and black screen on right](https://media.appleinsider.com/gallery/68445-144289-68124-143594-67400-141876-iphone18procolorarray-xl-xl-(1)-xl.jpg)  
Apple's iPhone 18 Pro will feature numerous improvements over the iPhone 17 Pro.

  
Coming via a [post](https://weibo.com/7215797790/5337722051887774) on the Weibo social network, the leak claims that the A20 Pro's chip layout was reverse-engineered from its solder positions. This method allows the leaker to identify different aspects of the chip and make assumptions based on what they see.  
  
Based on the newly plotted layout, the leaker claims that the A20 Pro's efficiency CPU cores will have 8MB of L2 cache to share between them. That would represent an increase over the 6MB of cache offered to cores in the [iPhone 17](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone-17 "iPhone 17") Pro's A19 Pro.  
  
  
 **Rumor Score:** 🤯 Likely

entries.content:

The Anker MindBase is a smart home hub with Matter support and a built-in NAS - image credit: Anker.

  
Following a revision of its lineup in [January 2026](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/01/05/transform-your-charging-with-ankers-new-lineup-at-ces-2026), Anker has now announced a further series of cameras and sensors, plus the Anker MindBase smart home hub to control them all. entries.title: The plastic waste overtaking New York – and the people trying to curb it
entries.content:
From New York to Quebec, photographer Bryan Anselm spent months capturing spaces overrun with plastic and the actions individuals and groups are taking to reduce waste

In New York City, the plastic we discard has a way of remaining in plain sight. There are few alleys to hide residents’ refuse, and the clear recycling bags leave their contents on full display. In a city built on a dense grid, lightweight wrappers, bags and bottles spill from overflowing bins and skitter down sidewalks, collecting in gutters and corners before the wind carries them on.

All that plastic is a layer of the urban landscape, as familiar as subway grates and fire escapes, revealing a messy and unflattering aspect of city life. “Garbage is not what we cast out, but the prime locus of meaning in our lives,” the character Nick Shay says in Don DeLillo’s Underworld.

[Continue reading...](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/ng-interactive/2026/sep/03/plastic-waste-new-york-environment)

## Amazon Labor Day Deals FAQs

### When do Labor Day sales start?

Early [Labor Day sales](https://lifehacker.com/labor-day) have already started. More retailers are likely to start their own sales leading up to the holiday on Monday, Sept. 7.

### Are Labor Day sales worth it?

Labor Day has traditionally been a good time to find deals in many categories, but whether they're worth it or not depends entirely on what you're looking for. Compared to sales like Black Friday or Prime Day, Labor Day falls short on volume and quality of discounts, but you might still find a good price on tech or kitchen appliances that will match those holiday prices—or even beat them. (We use [price tracking tools](https://lifehacker.com/best-price-tracking-tools-1692745053) to let you know if a deal is worth it or not.)

SEE 3 MORE

[LG’s 32-inch UltraGear 32GX870A-B](https://zdcs.link/aBoyRB?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=LG%E2%80%99s%2032-inch%20UltraGear%2032GX870A-B&object_type=content&short_url=aBoyRB&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is $814.46 (originally $1,399.99), making it the deal I’d pick for someone building a high-end gaming setup but who still wants a monitor that works well outside competitive games. Its OLED panel can run at 4K up to 240Hz, then switch to 1080p at up to 480Hz, so you can favor sharper visuals for single-player games or more speed when playing something competitive. The near-instant 0.03ms response time and OLED’s deep blacks also make this the strongest picture-quality option in the group.

[LG’s 27-inch UltraGear 27GX790B-B](https://zdcs.link/9gJDBG?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=LG%E2%80%99s%2027-inch%20UltraGear%2027GX790B-B&object_type=content&short_url=9gJDBG&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is $679.99 (originally $999.99), its lowest price yet according to [price trackers](https://lifehacker.com/best-price-tracking-tools), and this is the monitor I’d look at specifically for competitive gaming. Its OLED panel runs at QHD up to 540Hz and can push as high as 720Hz at a lower HD resolution, paired with a 0.02ms response time, according to the manufacturer. That level of speed is excessive for casual gaming, but it makes considerably more sense for someone playing esports titles where motion clarity and responsiveness take priority over 4K resolution.

[LG’s 34-inch UltraGear 34GX90SA-W](https://zdcs.link/akjMLg?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=LG%E2%80%99s%2034-inch%20UltraGear%2034GX90SA-W&object_type=content&short_url=akjMLg&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is $699.99 (originally $1,099.99) and takes a different approach with a 34-inch curved OLED ultrawide. Its 3440-by-1440 display runs at 240Hz with a 0.03ms response time, giving games more horizontal room while keeping the speed you’d expect from a premium gaming monitor. That said, its 800R curve wraps closely around your field of view, so it’s best suited to someone who likes sitting close to an immersive screen—and its built-in webOS also means it can handle streaming without needing the PC switched on.

[LG’s 27-inch UltraGear 27G850A-B](https://zdcs.link/avAk6q?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=LG%E2%80%99s%2027-inch%20UltraGear%2027G850A-B&object_type=content&short_url=avAk6q&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is $599.99 (originally $899.99) and is the one I’d choose if you want high-end gaming performance but would rather stick with IPS than OLED. Its 4K Nano IPS Black panel runs at 240Hz, with the option to switch to 1080p at 480Hz, and DisplayPort 2.1 gives a compatible PC enough bandwidth for those higher-resolution, higher-refresh-rate combinations. You don’t get OLED’s perfect blacks, but there’s also no OLED burn-in concern.

[LG’s 37-inch UltraGear 37G800A-B](https://zdcs.link/QVJwZ3?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=LG%E2%80%99s%2037-inch%20UltraGear%2037G800A-B&object_type=content&short_url=QVJwZ3&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is $590 (originally $799.99) and makes the most sense if physical screen size is higher on your list than chasing the fastest refresh rate possible. Its 37-inch curved 4K VA panel runs at 165Hz, giving you substantially more screen space than the 27-inch options while still being fast enough for most gaming. Labor Day has traditionally been a good time to find deals in many categories, but whether they're worth it or not depends entirely on what you're looking for. entries.title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: New features, release date, beta, compatible Macs
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

Apple has already revealed many of the new features coming in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the next major update for the Mac. Headline changes include an all-new Siri AI assistant, major upgrades to apps including Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail and Calendar, expanded child-safety features, design refinements and performance improvements throughout the operating system. We’ve also had the chance to see many of these features in action through the beta, with the full release now likely to be only days away.

Golden Gate continues Apple’s tradition of naming macOS releases after iconic Californian landmarks. More broadly, the update represents another step in Apple’s push to make the Mac smarter and more proactive, with greater use of Apple Intelligence across the operating system and a stronger focus on helping users complete everyday tasks more quickly.

macOS 27 will support all Macs powered by Apple silicon, marking the end of the road for Intel-based Macs. While Intel models won’t be eligible for the new operating system, Apple is expected to continue providing security updates for them for some time.

Apple made [developer and public betas of macOS 27 available](https://www.macworld.com/article/671123/should-i-install-macos-beta-latest-version.html), with the finished version expected in September 2026. This hub covers everything you need to know about macOS 27 Golden Gate, including its new features, compatibility, beta releases and Apple Intelligence upgrades.

## What’s New in macOS 27 Golden Gate at a glance

![WWDC 2026 macOS Features](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/WWDC-2026-macOS-Features.png?w=1200)

Apple

Here are the top ten new features and changes coming with macOS 27 Golden Gate.

1. **Siri AI**: A redesigned conversational Siri that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access the web and take actions across apps.
2. **Apple Intelligence**: Systemwide proofreading, smarter writing tools, improved dictation and automatic file and folder naming.
3. **Safari upgrades**: Automatic tab grouping, webpage change alerts with Notify Me, AI-generated extensions and faster, more efficient browsing.
4. **Smarter Messages and Mail**: Personalized Smart Reply, better search and syncing, contextual suggestions and improved reliability.
5. **New Photos tools**: Spatial Reframing, image expansion with Extend, improved Clean Up and better search and organisation.
6. **More powerful built-in apps**: New features for Passwords, Calendar, Notes, Preview, Freeform, Weather, Shortcuts and Image Playground.
7. **Expanded parental controls**: Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time, contact approvals and broader Communication Safety protections.
8. **Better Mac gaming**: Game Porting Toolkit 4 promises significant performance and compatibility improvements for Windows games.
9. **Refined Liquid Glass design**: Better readability and consistency, adjustable transparency, cleaner Finder windows and improved iPhone Mirroring.
10. **Faster macOS performance**: Quicker app launches, Spotlight, AirDrop and networking, plus improved external-display, Thunderbolt and Bluetooth support.

## macOS 27 release date: When will macOS 27 be available?

* General release TBC, we predict September 14.

In recent years, Apple has released macOS around the same time as iOS, typically on the Monday following its [September iPhone launch event](https://www.macworld.com/article/831417/apple-september-iphone-event-date-time.html). With Apple’s 2026 keynote taking place on Wednesday, September 9, our best guess is that macOS 27 will be released on **Monday, September 14**.

## macOS 27 Beta – What’s new in the latest beta?

* Latest beta: Beta 8, August 31, 2026

![Apple Beta](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Apple-Beta.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple

Apple released the first macOS 27 developer beta at WWDC, followed by the first public beta on July 13, 2026. The current version is developer beta 8, released on August 31, alongside Public Beta 6.

At this late stage, Apple is mainly refining the software ahead of its expected September release. Recent betas focus on Siri AI, faster performance and search, Safari automation, deeper Apple Intelligence integration and further refinements to Liquid Glass.

Most people should still wait for the final release, particularly if they rely on their Mac for work or use specialist software. Beta software can still cause crashes, app compatibility problems, increased battery drain and, in some cases, data loss. If you do install it, make a full backup first and ideally use a secondary Mac, separate volume or external SSD.

Here’s how you can [participate in the beta program](https://www.macworld.com/article/671123/how-to-install-macos-beta.html) we also recommend reading our guide to [whether you should install the latest macOS beta](https://www.macworld.com/article/671123/should-i-install-macos-beta-latest-version.html).

Separately, the macOS 26.7 release candidate appears to have [revealed a substantial part of Apple’s upcoming hardware roadmap](https://www.macworld.com/article/3214949/upcoming-apple-products-revealed-in-macos-26-7-release-candidate.html), with references to nearly 40 products, including the iPhone Ultra, iPhone 18 range, M6 and OLED MacBook Pros, new iMacs and iPads. Other references point to camera-equipped AirPods, new Home devices, a security camera, tabletop robot, next-generation Vision Pro and further undisclosed products.

## Siri AI: Siri powered macOS 27 features

![Siri AI waitlist macOS 27](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/siri-AI-waitlist.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foiundry

Apple’s biggest focus in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Siri AI, a completely redesigned version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence. Rather than functioning primarily as a voice assistant, Siri is becoming a conversational AI that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access current information from the web and take actions across apps.

We [tested Siri AI in beta on a MacBook Neo](https://www.macworld.com/article/3161306/im-using-macos-golden-gates-siri-on-the-macbook-neo-ask-us-anything.html), and it behaves much more like a generative-AI chatbot than the Siri of old. It can answer questions directly, understand natural follow-ups and solve problems instead of simply directing users to web searches.

### At a glance: What’s new with Siri AI?

**Conversational AI assistant**: Siri can handle open-ended questions, brainstorming, research and natural back-and-forth conversations.

**Dedicated Siri app**: A standalone Siri app keeps conversations in one place and syncs them through iCloud, allowing users to start a conversation on one Apple device and continue it on another.

**Personal context awareness**: Siri will be able to understand information in Messages, Mail, Notes, Photos, Maps and files to locate information and provide answers based on your personal data.

**Web-powered answers**: Siri can access current information from the web, making it more useful for research, learning, interview preparation and questions about recent events.

**App actions and automation**: Siri can perform tasks across apps such as Messages, Music, Reminders, Calendar and Maps using natural-language instructions.

**Spotlight integration**: Siri AI is integrated with Spotlight, allowing users to type questions and receive AI-generated answers without opening a browser or separate app.

**Visual Intelligence**: Visual Intelligence comes to the Mac for the first time, allowing Siri to understand selected images, documents, files, text and other content displayed on screen.

![macOS 27 Golden Gate Visual Intelligence](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/VisualIntelligence.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Apple’s Visual Intelligence initially placed Blutenburg in Denmark.

Macwelt

**Writing Tools**: Siri can generate text, rewrite drafts, summarise content and adjust wording or tone. Apple says it can also adapt writing to the way you typically communicate with particular contacts.

**Improved dictation**: Systemwide dictation gains better speech recognition along with automatic punctuation, capitalisation and formatting.

**Custom Siri voices**: Users can choose Siri’s voice and adjust characteristics such as pace and expressiveness, although some of these capabilities require newer hardware.

macOS 27 also contains an experimental [Siri AI popover](https://www.macworld.com/article/3194935/macos-27-has-a-secret-popover-menu-for-ai-power-users.html) seen in the beta. Selecting text can bring up a small Siri icon offering contextual actions including Writing Tools, summaries and key points, sending messages or emails, creating calendar events, opening locations in Maps, and tracking flights or packages. The feature is not currently enabled by default and requires Apple’s FeatureFlags system to activate, suggesting it may still be under development.

Apple also appears to be taking a relatively restrained approach to AI behaviour. [In our testing](https://www.macworld.com/article/3164693/siri-ai-is-both-impressive-and-disappointing.html), Siri avoids presenting itself as human, excessive flattery and potentially harmful responses, while generally keeping its answers straightforward.

## When will Siri AI be available on Mac?

Siri AI is already available in beta, and Apple says it will be released to the public “later this year.” We therefore expect it to arrive as an update to macOS 27 and Apple’s other OS 27 releases rather than as part of the initial launch.

Apple has also said Siri AI will still be labelled as a beta when it launches, so users should expect some rough edges and continued improvements after release.

Siri AI is initially available in English. Availability will vary by region. Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the European Union because of issues related to the Digital Markets Act, and it will remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory approvals. However, it will be available on [Mac and Vision Pro in the EU](https://www.macworld.com/article/3182183/constructive-siri-ai-meeting-sparks-hope-for-iphone-users-overseas.html).

## Which Macs support Siri AI?

Siri AI requires a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence, but some of its most advanced capabilities have higher hardware requirements.

Apple says its most powerful on-device AI model, expressive Siri voices and advanced dictation require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory. Macs that support Apple Intelligence but do not meet those requirements can still receive other Siri AI features, although the exact feature set may vary.

## Safari features coming in macOS 27

![safari notify me popup](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/safari-notify-me-popup.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Notify Me in Safari

Apple

Safari is getting several Apple Intelligence-powered upgrades in macOS 27, including smarter tab organisation, webpage monitoring, custom extension generation and performance improvements.

* **Automatic Tab Topics**: Safari will automatically group related tabs by topic as you browse, helping keep research and projects organised. These groups can also be saved for later.
* **Notify Me**: Safari will be able to [monitor webpages for changes and alert you](https://www.macworld.com/article/3159801/my-fingers-already-love-this-macos-27-safari-feature.html) when something happens, such as a product coming back in stock or a price dropping, removing the need to keep refreshing pages manually.
* **Describe an Extension**: Users will be able to create custom Safari extensions simply by describing what they want. Safari will generate the extension from the text description and add it to the toolbar.
* **Faster, more efficient browsing**: Apple says Safari will use less power while improving page-loading speed, JavaScript performance, scrolling, animations and resizing of the Start Page.

![Browser Alarm macOS 27 Golden Gate](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/browseralarm.jpg?quality=50&strip=all)

Get notified.

Macwelt

## Messages and Mail features coming in macOS 27

Messages and Mail are gaining deeper Apple Intelligence integration in macOS 27, alongside improvements to search, syncing and everyday reliability.

### Messages

* **One-Tap Suggestions in Messages**: Messages will suggest useful actions based on the context of a conversation, such as creating a reminder or note without leaving the chat.
* **Smarter Photo Suggestions**: Messages will surface relevant photos based on people, places and keywords mentioned in a conversation.
* **Personalized Smart Reply**: Suggested replies can reflect your usual writing style and adapt depending on who you’re messaging.
* **Improved syncing**: Messages should sync more reliably across devices, while failed messages will automatically retry sending.

### Mail

* **Personalized Smart Reply**: Mail will also generate suggested responses that better match your writing style and the person you’re replying to.
* **More relevant search**: A new ranking system will prioritise the most useful search results, alongside improved search indexing.
* **Faster and more accurate**: Apple says Mail will load messages more quickly and provide more reliable unread counts.

## Photos features coming in macOS 27

Photos is gaining new AI-powered editing and organisation tools in macOS 27, making it easier to improve images, find photos and manage an iCloud library.

* **Spatial Reframing**: Photos will be able to intelligently recompose and reframe images after they’ve been taken.
* **Extend Tool**: A new Extend tool can expand an image beyond its original boundaries, filling in missing areas when changing the crop or aspect ratio.
* **Enhanced Clean Up**: Apple’s Clean Up tool will be better at removing larger unwanted objects and distractions from photos.
* **Better organisation and search**: Photos adds keywords, star ratings, improved metadata search and other tools for organising a library.
* **Faster iCloud syncing**: iCloud Photos can begin uploads more quickly, with an option to prioritise syncing when needed.

## Other new features coming to apps with macOS 27

macOS 27 also brings a wide range of smaller upgrades across Apple’s built-in apps, with a particular focus on automation, organisation, security and Apple Intelligence.

### Passwords

The Passwords app can automatically identify weak or compromised passwords and, with Apple Intelligence, visit supported websites, change the password and save the new credentials. This could remove much of the manual work involved in updating large numbers of old or leaked passwords, although questions remain over website compatibility, two-factor authentication and how consistently the feature will work. Read: [Apple finally got rid of my biggest password headache.](https://www.macworld.com/article/3160935/apple-finally-got-rid-of-my-biggest-password-headache.html)

### Image Playground

Image Playground gets a substantial AI upgrade, including the ability to create photorealistic images and make more convincing edits to existing pictures, such as changing colours, hair and other details. Apple continues to apply safeguards around real people, copyrighted characters and distinctive artistic styles.

![macOS Golden Gate Image Playground](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/macos-golden-gate-image-playground.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

### Calendar

Calendar gains natural-language event creation, making it possible to describe an event rather than manually entering every detail. It can also make changes to multiple events at once.

### Preview

Preview supports more document formats, improves PDF editing and saves PDF files more quickly.

### Notes

Notes gains [drawing tools for sketching](https://www.macworld.com/article/3183430/macos-27-golden-gate-ai-features-freeform-image-playground-notes-weather.html) with a mouse or trackpad, along with digital signatures, Markdown copy-and-paste and links to sections within notes.

![macos golden gate notes drawing tools](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/macos-golden-gate-notes-drawing-tools.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Notes now features a drawing tool as well as the ability to create and use digital signatures.

Foundry

### Freeform

Freeform adds drawing tools, collaborative folders and improved organisation, including the ability to sort boards into folders. Full dark-mode support also changes the appearance of the drawing canvas.

![macOS Golden Gate Freeform boards](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/macOS-GOlden-Gate-Freeform-boards.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

In Freeform, boards can now be organised into folders.

Foundry

### Weather

Weather gets a clearer and more detailed forecast interface, with reorganised information tiles and enhanced 10-day forecasts showing precipitation probability and amount, as well as wind speeds throughout the day.

![macOS golden gate weather](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/macOS-golden-gate-weather.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

In the Weather app, the tiles have been rearranged, and there are separate 10-day forecasts for precipitation and wind (circled in red).

Foundry

### Shortcuts

Shortcuts gains a redesigned editor, more automation capabilities and one of macOS 27’s more ambitious AI features: the ability to turn natural-language instructions into working automations.

![macOS Golden Gate automatischer Kurzbefehl](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Automatischer-Kurzbefehl.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Shortcuts can start automatically when a specific event occurs.

Thomas Armbrüster

### Parental Controls

Apple is expanding its family-safety tools with Safari’s Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time and Time Allowances, contact approvals and broader Communication Safety protections. The changes [give parents more control over what children can access](https://www.macworld.com/article/3164257/how-macos-27-is-going-to-help-apple-sell-a-ton-more-macbook-neos.html) and who they can communicate with without completely locking down the Mac.

### Accessibility, Shared Albums and Suggestions

macOS 27 also includes accessibility improvements, expanded Shared Albums and more contextual Suggestions throughout the operating system.

### Game Porting Toolkit 4

Apple’s Game Porting Toolkit 4 arrives alongside macOS 27 and promises significant improvements for running and porting Windows games on Apple silicon Macs.

Early beta testing suggests [substantial performance gains](https://www.macworld.com/article/3189951/apples-latest-game-porting-toolkit-beta-changed-how-i-think-about-mac-gaming.html). On an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, GTA V reportedly increased from around 106fps to 176fps, while Red Dead Redemption 2 improved from roughly 60fps to 75fps.

The results suggest software compatibility, rather than raw Apple silicon performance, is increasingly the main obstacle to better Mac gaming. Improvements to Game Porting Toolkit could make Windows titles more practical to run and easier for developers to bring to macOS.

## Design and Interface Changes in macOS 27

![macOS 27 SIri ](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/image_815009.png?w=1200)

Apple

macOS 27 Golden Gate refines the Liquid Glass redesign introduced in macOS 26, with Apple focusing on readability, consistency and usability rather than another major visual overhaul.

Changes include:

* **Improved Liquid Glass**: Stronger contrast, better readability and more consistent refraction effects across windows, menus and controls.
* **Customisable transparency**: Users can adjust the Liquid Glass effect in System Settings, from a clearer appearance to a more heavily tinted look.
* **Cleaner Finder and toolbars**: Finder sidebars are more clearly defined, toolbars are more consistent, and edge-to-edge sidebars replace some of the floating elements introduced in macOS 26.
* **More consistent windows**: Window corners, controls and active-window highlighting have been standardised to make the interface feel more coherent.
* **Updated icons and menus**: Menu-bar and app icons gain sharper outlines, improved contrast and more depth, while unnecessary menu icons have been reduced.
* **Smoother window management**: Mission Control and Spaces animations have been refined, and active windows should be easier to distinguish.
* **New wallpapers and screensavers**: Golden Gate-themed backgrounds include animated daytime and nighttime views of the bridge.
* **Swipe to refresh**: Supported Mac apps gain a swipe-down-to-refresh gesture.
* **Improved iPhone Mirroring**: iPhone Mirroring adds Control Center access, resizable app windows and support for DRM-protected video.

![macos 27 golden gate wallpaper](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/macos-27-golden-gate-wallpaper.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Foundry

## Performance improvements and system changes in macOS 27

Apple says macOS 27 focuses on speed, efficiency and everyday usability, with improvements across apps, networking, displays and system tasks. Most of these changes do not require Apple Intelligence.

Changes include:

* **Faster overall performance**: Apps should launch more quickly, while an optimised CPU scheduler improves system responsiveness.
* **Faster Spotlight and setup**: Spotlight indexing and new user-account creation are quicker.
* **Faster file transfers and networking**: AirDrop and network file browsing are faster, while Ethernet status can appear in the menu bar.
* **Thunderbolt and Bluetooth improvements**: RDMA over Thunderbolt has been improved, alongside more efficient Bluetooth power management.
* **Faster Safari**: The Safari Start Page loads more quickly, with broader browser performance improvements.
* **Better external-display support**: New high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes include 5K at 120Hz, alongside improved display-position persistence, HDR support for the macOS interface and 5K Mac mirroring.

Apple Intelligence powered changes:

* **AI-powered file naming – requires Apple Intelligence**: macOS can suggest filenames and folder names based on their contents, including in Pages, Numbers, TextEdit and Finder.
* **Systemwide proofreading **– requires Apple Intelligence****: Apple Intelligence provides automatic proofreading and improved spelling and grammar suggestions throughout macOS.

**Apple Intelligence privacy**: Apple says AI processing happens on-device where possible, with Private Cloud Compute used for more demanding tasks. Data processed in the cloud is not stored or made accessible to Apple.

## macOS 27 Compatible Macs

![MacBook Neo 2026](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/macbook-neo-angle.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

The MacBook Neo and other Macs in Apple’s current lineup will all be compatible with macOS 27.

Foundry

Apple confirmed that macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with:

* MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, 2026)
* MacBook Air (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
* MacBook Pro (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
* iMac (Apple silicon, 2021 and later)
* Mac mini (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
* Mac Studio (2022 and later)
* Mac Pro (Apple silicon, 2023 and later)

All supported Macs can run Apple Intelligence, although some of the most advanced Siri AI features require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory.

## What about Intel Macs?

macOS 27 marks another major step in Apple’s transition away from Intel. macOS 26 Tahoe was the final version to support Intel Macs, and Apple is now [encouraging developers to remove Intel code](https://www.macworld.com/article/3225932/apple-to-mac-developers-its-time-to-let-go-of-intel.html) from their apps and focus on Apple silicon.

macOS 27 will also be the [final version to support Rosetta](https://www.macworld.com/article/3063982/apple-ends-rosetta-support-macos-28.html), Apple’s translation technology for running Intel-only apps on Apple silicon Macs. Those apps will continue to work in macOS 27, but will stop working in macOS 28 unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions.

To help users prepare, macOS 27 includes an Intel-app checker in System Settings that lists Intel-based apps used during the past year. If you still rely on any essential Intel-only software, now is a good time to look for updates or alternatives before upgrading to macOS 28.

## What happens to DVD support?

macOS 27 also begins the [phase-out of Apple’s native DVD support](https://www.macworld.com/article/3182344/macos-27-golden-gate-marks-the-end-of-built-in-dvd-support.html). Apple has removed the DVDPlayback framework from the macOS 27 SDK and says it will disappear completely in a future version of macOS.  
Golden Gate may still include the DVD Player app, but it is likely to be the last macOS release with Apple’s built-in DVD playback support. Users who still watch DVDs on a Mac will increasingly need to rely on third-party software such as VLC.

## FAQ

---

1.

### When will macOS 27 Golden Gate be released?

Apple hasn’t confirmed exactly when macOS 27 will be available to install, but it usually launches to the general public in September, or at the latest October.

Once macOS 27 launches Apple will likely continue beta development to test new features that weren’t available at launch.

2.

### Should I install the macOS 27 beta?

Whether you should install the macOS 27 beta depends on your needs, technical expertise, and tolerance for bugs and instability. Beta software can introduce crashes, data loss, app compatibility problems, excessive battery drain, reduced performance, and other unexpected issues.

For most users, the recommendation is simple: don’t install it. If you’re eager to try the new features download the Public Beta – but avoid installing it on your primary Mac.

Developers are a different case. The Developer Beta is available now through Apple’s Developer Program, allowing app creators to test their software against new APIs, frameworks, and system features before the public release. If you’re not a developer, think carefully before installing the Developer Beta, as it is typically less stable and more prone to bugs than later beta releases.

Regardless of which beta you choose, make sure you have a complete backup of your Mac before upgrading.

3.

### Which Macs can run macOS 27?

All M-series Macs will get macOS 27, and the MacBook Neo.

Certain Siri AI features – most powerful on-device model, expressive voices and advanced dictation – will only be available for M3 Macs and newer.

4.

### Should Intel Mac owners upgrade now?

Intel Mac owners should upgrade to Apple Silicon as soon as possible. The transition away from Intel hardware has reached a critical turning point, with software support rapidly vanishing and a new generation of affordable entry-level hardware making the switch more accessible than ever.

Apple has confirmed that macOS 27 will not support any Intel-based Macs. While a small number of Intel models may receive security patches for older versions of macOS until September 2028, they are already excluded from modern flagship features.

Those with Intel Macs also miss out on many features, including Apple Intelligence.

5.

### Will macOS 27 support Rosetta and Intel apps?

macOS 27 will still run Intel-only Mac apps through Rosetta 2. However, macOS 27 will be the final version of macOS to support Rosetta 2 as a general-purpose translation technology for running Intel-based Mac apps on Apple silicon.

Rosetta has acted as a transition layer since Apple introduced its own Mac chips in 2020, translating x86\_64 Intel instructions so older software can run on Apple silicon. After macOS 27, most Intel-only Mac apps will no longer work unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions, although Apple will retain limited Rosetta functionality for some older, unmaintained games.

Apple is already preparing users for the change. Since macOS 26.4, Macs can display warnings when launching apps that rely on Rosetta, encouraging users to update to Apple silicon-native versions before general Rosetta support ends.

In macOS 28, most Intel-only apps will no longer run unless developers update them for Apple silicon.

6.

### When is macOS usually updated?

Here is a history of release dates for macOS:

* macOS 26 Tahoe: September 15, 2025
* macOS 15 Sequoia: September 16, 2024
* macOS 14 Sonoma: September 26, 2023

entries.title: Dreames new robot lawn mower has a swing arm to make for precise edges
entries.content:
![the Roborock A4 AWD Pro robot lawn mower working outside](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/04dMcTUhg2A9dd5fHq61Jit/hero-image.png)

One of the world's largest consumer technology shows kicks off on Friday, and [Dreame](https://mashable.com/article/what-is-dreame-brand) understood the assignment. IFA is all-in on the robot lawn mowers this year and Dreame has a new model that's set to enter the market in 2027. The brand has been one of Mashable's favorite options for [robot vacuums](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-robot-vacuums-2026-tested) in the last few years and their lineup of robot lawn mowers is getting damn impressive. Welcome to the yard, Dreame A4 AWD Pro Series.

## A robot lawn mower with a swing arm

Like robot vacuums, the majority of robot lawn mowers set out to do the same task: rid us of the inconvenience of manually mowing the lawn. But now that the market has a handful of top models and brands, things are starting to get fancier.

The new Dreame A4 AWD Pro Series is the brand's introductory model made with the EdgeMaster 4.0 Precision Edge-Trimming System. This enables a swing arm to extend the standard cutting disc outward as the mower senses nearby boundaries. After playing with a few robot lawn mowers, I can say this will be a major benefit since not all robots are comfortable getting close to the edge. At times, I've gone out with the string trimmer to get a cleaner line around the edge.

SEE ALSO:
[The Roborock RockNeo Q110H robot lawn mower just landed at Amazon, and it's on sale for just 1 week](https://mashable.com/life/roborock-rockneo-q110h-robot-lawn-mower-release)

Of course, the Dreame does this while still saying a safe distance away from walls, fences, or flower beds, but the zero centimeter edge cutting is a unique feature that makes using a robot lawn mower and truly hands-off experience.

In addition to the arm, the Dreame AWD can handle climbing slopes that measure up to 90% or 42 degrees. It can also glide over holes or divots of about four inches deep and six inches wide.

## Advanced navigation and intelligence

Since the little robot is sent out to mow on its own, it relies on a solid navigation system. The new Dreame AWD uses a slew of tech to make this happen like 360-degree 3D LiDAR, satellite and network Omni RTK, and AI-powered binocular vision. The infrared sensor can help keep the mower away from people and pets.

## How to buy the Dreame A4 AWD Pro Series

At the time of launch, Dreame's press release mentions the new robot mower will hit global markets in the first half of 2027. Starting price (listed in Euros) translates to about $3,500, but pricing can vary by market so we could see a different price in the U.S. We do have details that two models of the A4 AWD Pro will launch with one being suitable for almost an acre and the other model capable of mowing about 1.2 acres.

If you're looking for a Dreame robot lawn mower that's already on the market, the [Dreame LiDAR 3500 Robot Lawn Mower A3 AWD](https://zdcs.link/91MMp8?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Dreame%20LiDAR%203500%20Robot%20Lawn%20Mower%20A3%20AWD&object_type=article&object_uuid=04dMcTUhg2A9dd5fHq61Jit&short_url=91MMp8&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)") is on sale at Amazon for $2,399.99, down from the list price of $2,999.99.

entries.title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on September 3
entries.content:
![An image of a full moon.](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/05wnx2VNbY9V9kumHFZMSj2/hero-image.jpg)

The Full Moon wasn't that long ago, but already it's looking a lot different. Its fully illuminated face is shrinking night by night as it moves into the next phase of its lunar cycle.

## What is today’s Moon phase?

As of Thursday, Sept. 3, [NASA's Daily Moon Guide](https://moon.nasa.gov/moon-observation/daily-moon-guide/?intent=011#1767622046258::0::) tracker tells us the [Moon](https://mashable.com/article/ispace-moon-lander-south-pole-image) is in Waning Gibbous phase, with 62% of its surface visible.

Without visual aids, tonight you can see the Copernicus and Tycho craters and the Oceanus Procellarum. If you have binoculars, you'll be able to spot the Grimaldi Basin, Alphonsus Crater and Clavius Crater. Finally, with a telescope you'll also see the Apollo 14 landing spot and the Schiller Crater.

## When is the next Full Moon?

The next Full Moon will take place on September 26.

## What are Moon phases?

The Moon's appearance gradually changes as it travels around Earth, completing a full lunar cycle in approximately 29.5 days, [NASA](https://www.nasa.gov) tells us. What we see from Earth depends on the Moon's position in relation to the Sun, which affects how much of its illuminated side is visible. As the cycle progresses, the Moon passes through a series of phases, from a thin crescent to a half Moon and then a Full Moon, before starting over.

The eight phases are:

New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it’s not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere)

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

entries.title: Learning to Code in the Age of AI: Advice From a Top Udemy Instructor
entries.content:
*What should a beginner developer learn in order to keep up in the AI era? This is one of the most debated questions in tech right now. We got in touch with **[Ardit Sulce](http://linkedin.com/in/arditsulce)**, a Python educator with over 650,000 students on Udemy, and talked about the value of struggling when learning something new, the changing role of teachers, the skills junior developers need, and why students should learn with professional development tools from the very beginning.*

![](https://blog.jetbrains.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/final-profile-pic.png)

#### Ardit Sulce is a Python programmer and top Udemy instructor with 10 years of teaching experience.

He holds a master’s degree in Geospatial Technologies from the University of Münster, Germany. Ardit is also the founder and main developer of [ActiveSkill Dev](https://www.activeskill.dev/) – a platform for learning coding and software development with AI as a personal tutor. Ardit believes that the best way to learn Python is by building real applications. His courses combine beginner-friendly explanations with hands-on exercises using professional tools – from automation scripts to AI agents.

## **In this interview, we cover topics such as:**

* How AI is changing the role of teachers
* When beginners should “tough it out” and when they should use AI
* Three skills junior developers need in the AI era
* Why you should learn in a professional IDE
* A three-stage path for learning to program with AI

## **The teacher’s role in the AI era**

**Q: Ardit, you taught programming before generative AI became part of the everyday development workflow. How have students’ expectations of learning programming changed?**

**Ardit Sulce:** I teach programming mainly through video content. You’re not just hearing what a virtual environment is; you’re watching someone create one, activate it, and use it in real time. That format still works, and students still love it.

What has changed in the world of AI, though, is the number of questions I receive from students. I get 5–10 times fewer questions a day than I did before. When students get stuck, they just go to AI and get answers in seconds. Before, they would post the question in the course Q&A and wait hours for me or a teaching assistant to respond. That waiting is gone, so they stay in the flow of learning instead of stopping at every obstacle. The questions that still reach me tend to be the bigger ones: *Which path should I take?* *Is this project good enough for my portfolio?* *How does this fit into the larger picture?* etc.

> “*AI absorbed the small questions, and what’s left for the teacher are the ones that actually require judgment.*”

![](https://blog.jetbrains.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/final-profile-pic.png)

There’s one more expectation that’s new. Students now expect AI to be part of the curriculum. Before AI, a Python course was about Python. Today, learners want to know how Python and AI fit together, how to use AI tools to write code faster, but also how to build things with AI: apps that use language models, agents, automations.

A course that ignores AI feels outdated to them, and rightly so. That’s the biggest shift I’ve had to make as an instructor – not in how I teach, but in what I teach.

**Q: If AI can answer those small questions instantly, what remains of the role of a programming course and teacher?**

**Ardit Sulce:** As mentioned earlier, students can get answers to their questions instantly. However, when you know nothing about a topic, you don’t know what to ask. This is where a teacher is still crucial. A beginner doesn’t know that virtual environments exist, so they’ll never ask about them. They don’t know what they don’t know.

> “*The role of a course is exactly this: It’s a curated path through a territory the student has never seen.* ”

![](https://blog.jetbrains.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/final-profile-pic.png)

AI is phenomenal at answering questions, but someone still has to know what questions are worth asking, and in what order. That’s the teacher’s job.

We always had good and bad teachers in school. Both had the same books and the same blackboard, yet with one of them the hour flew by, and with the other you counted the minutes. The good ones had an energy that made you curious to listen. This seems to be hard for AI to replicate.

## **When struggling helps you learn**

**Q: Learning to program has always involved frustration. Which parts of the struggle should AI remove, and which should it preserve? How can beginners tell the difference?**

> “*The keyword here is ‘struggle’. Learning has to be a struggle. If there is no struggle, you can’t learn anything.* ”

![](https://blog.jetbrains.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/final-profile-pic.png)

The mind has to struggle to absorb something new. You can take a programming book and read it casually at the beach, but you’re not going to learn anything from it.

> “*You need to take that book, open the IDE, and put in the work – replicate the results from the book, experiment with the code, fail, and try to find what’s wrong with your code. It’s only then that you learn anything.* ”

![](https://blog.jetbrains.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/final-profile-pic.png)

The confusion, the error messages, the twenty minutes spent on a missing colon – that’s not an obstacle to learning. That *is* learning.

One thing is for sure, though: Typing code by hand is going to be a thing of the past – but only among professionals. For students, the only way to understand programming is to do things by hand first. You need to write syntax to understand what you are doing. So the struggle of manually typing code is worth preserving for students, but worth eliminating for pros. It’s not about the task; it’s about what stage you’re at.

So how can a beginner tell the difference between struggle that teaches and struggle that just wastes time? My rule of thumb is simple: If the struggle is about understanding, keep it; if it’s just friction, remove it. Struggling to understand why your loop runs one time too many? Keep going – that’s how you learn. Fighting a broken driver installation, a cryptic setup error, or an outdated tutorial? Let AI handle it. There’s no lesson there.

Ask yourself, *once I get past this, will I understand programming better, or will I just be back where I started?* If solving the problem teaches you something you’ll reuse, struggle through it yourself. If it’s a one-time roadblock, hand it to AI. Beginners tend to get this exactly backward. They let AI write the loop, then spend an evening fighting the driver. It should be the other way around.

**Q: If working code is no longer sufficient proof of learning, what should educators and employers look for instead?**

**Ardit Sulce:** Honestly, working code was never good proof. It was just the cheapest thing to measure. Students copied from Stack Overflow long before ChatGPT existed, and every teacher knew it. AI didn’t create the problem. It just made the shortcut so fast and so clean that we can’t ignore it anymore.

The first thing I look for is whether the student can explain the code – not with formal terminology, just plain questions: *Why is this a dictionary and not a list?* *What happens if this file doesn’t exist?* *Why is this chunk of code inside a function?* *What would break if I moved this line above that one?* If a student used AI to write the code but can answer questions like these, they learned something. If they can’t, they merely “delivered” something.

I’d advise employers to do roughly the same thing. Stop asking job candidates to build; ask them to review. Hand them a file of AI-generated code with a subtle problem in it – an off-by-one, a silent exception swallow, a function that works but does the wrong thing on empty input – and see whether they notice and how they explain it. Or sit with them and debug something face-to-face. Watching how a person narrows down a problem tells you more in twenty minutes than any take-home assignment ever did.

## **Skills junior developers need in the AI era**

### **Q: What skills will help early-career developers stand out?**

**Ardit Sulce:** I would focus on three.

#### **1. Reading code you didn’t write**

Writing is cheap now; *judging* is the job. You’ll spend your days looking at code that came out of a model and deciding whether it’s good, does what you asked, and holds up when the input triples. Most beginners have never really read code – they’ve only written it. Flip that around: Read codebases on GitHub, revisit your old projects, and read what the agent produces instead of blindly accepting it.

#### **2. Saying precisely what you want**

We used to write programming. Now we “speak” programming, and most people are terrible at speaking it. They say, *build me a login system*, get something generic, and blame the model. A good prompt is a specification: what the code does, what it must not do, what happens at the edges. We used to call this “requirements”, and it used to be someone else’s job. Now it’s the main interface.

#### **3. System-level understanding**

And the third is exactly that system-level understanding I described above – knowing what an app is made of and how the pieces fit together. There’s no shortcut here, and that’s why it’s the differentiator.

> “*The first two make you productive with AI; the third is what makes you the person AI works for, instead of the other way around.*”

![](https://blog.jetbrains.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/final-profile-pic.png)

## **Learning with professional tools**

### **Q: Your latest video course, [Gen AI Engineer Bootcamp](https://www.udemy.com/course/ai-developer-bootcamp/), is paired with [hands-on practice in PyCharm](https://academy.jetbrains.com/course/32260). What can learning in a professional IDE add in the AI era?**

**Ardit Sulce:** Video is passive by nature. There’s a gap between *I watched someone do that* and *I can do that*. You have to get your hands dirty and code in an IDE. That’s why the [Gen AI Engineer Bootcamp Udemy video course](https://www.udemy.com/course/ai-developer-bootcamp/) is paired with hands-on practice in PyCharm – I didn’t want people to finish a lesson feeling like they understood it. I wanted them to immediately be in the same place I was, with the same tool, figuring things out firsthand.

There’s also a more practical reason.

> “*A gen AI engineer doesn’t work in a browser tab. They work with API keys in environment files, virtual environments, dependency conflicts, packages that break between versions, and agents that write files into their project. All of that lives in an IDE. If I teach the concepts but leave out the environment, I’ve taught half a job.*”

![](https://blog.jetbrains.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/final-profile-pic.png)

Then there’s what you get from writing, running, debugging, and modifying code – none of which a video can give you. Writing reveals which parts you only thought you understood. Running exposes you to the real environment: dependencies, virtual environments, package versions, configuration files, API keys, and tracebacks. Debugging teaches you to investigate instead of starting over. And modifying code shows whether you understand the project well enough to change it without breaking something else.

That final step is particularly important in the AI era. Generating an initial version of an application is becoming easier. Understanding existing code well enough to change it safely remains a real skill.

> “*There is also a practical reason to learn inside an IDE. AI coding agents work with actual projects and files. They create and modify code inside the development environment. If you are not comfortable navigating that environment, reviewing changes, running the project, and investigating problems, you are not really supervising the agent. You are only accepting what it produces.*”

![](https://blog.jetbrains.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/final-profile-pic.png)

[](https://blog.jetbrains.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/20260903-0825-38.2863097.mp4)

[Start the bootcamp in PyCharm](https://jb.gg/jy8jkn)

## **The new learning path for junior developers**

### **Q: Based on all of this, what should the learning path look like for someone starting today?**

**Ardit Sulce:** This question has concerned me since it became clear that generative AI could produce complete scripts. The interface is changing. Previously, developers expressed instructions mainly by writing programming languages. Now, they can also describe their intent in natural language and ask an agent to implement it. But programming is still the common denominator. You still need to understand how a program works, how data moves through it, how the components fit together, and how to determine whether the output is correct.

Syntax may be getting easier to produce. Understanding the system isn’t.

I would divide the learning path into three stages.

**1. Writing syntax by hand.** Write real code, i.e. small programs, in a proper IDE. Not because you’ll do this at work, but because this is where the mental model gets built: what a variable is, what a loop does, how data flows through a program. Don’t skip this stage.

**2. Using AI as a tutor.** Move to projects of increasing size, with AI explaining what you don’t understand along the way.

**3. Using AI as a co-worker.** Let AI write parts of the code while you review what it produces. Each project should be slightly bigger than the last: a script, then an app with a database, then something with users, something deployed, and something that talks to an API. That progression is what turns syntax knowledge into system knowledge.

The old way was to spend years mastering syntax and hope the architectural understanding shows up along the way. The new path is shorter but flipped: learn enough syntax to understand what’s happening, then focus on understanding systems – because that’s the part you’ll actually be paid for.

Manual coding is your homework while you’re still in the learning phase. Then, when you start your career, you’ll be ready for the architect’s work. Someone starting today isn’t at a disadvantage compared to those of us who spent twenty years coding manually. They’re skipping a stage that, frankly, was never the point.

We want to thank Ardit for sharing his experience and perspective on teaching and learning programming in the age of AI.

Are you a programming course creator interested in making your courses more hands-on with professional development tools? We’d love to explore ways to collaborate – whether you already use JetBrains IDEs or are considering bringing them into your teaching.

Through the [**JetBrains Course Creators Program**](https://www.jetbrains.com/academy/course-creators), we support educators with tools, resources, and opportunities to reach more learners. Explore the [JetBrains Course Creators Program](https://www.jetbrains.com/academy/course-creators) or contact us at [education@jetbrains.com](mailto:education@jetbrains.com).

entries.title: Cybercrooks trawl Fishbrain to net password hashes
entries.content: Cybercriminals have reeled in password hashes and corresponding salts belonging to users of popular fishing app Fishbrain, opening the door to cracking attempts. Fishbrain AB, which says its eponymous app serves more than 20 million anglers, disclosed the August 19 breach to the California Attorney General's Office this week. The unknown perpetrators helped themselves to a trawl of user data, including names, dates of birth, email addresses, phone numbers, Fishbrain usernames, country information, password hashes, and salts. "Fishbrain passwords were not stored in plaintext; however, Fishbrain has determined that the compromised password hashes for some users may be susceptible to being decoded," the company said in its disclosure [PDF]. It added: "If you use your Fishbrain password for any other online accounts, you should promptly update those passwords and any associated security questions or answers. "You should also take other appropriate steps to protect any online accounts that use the same username or email address and password combination. We recommend using a strong, unique password for each of your accounts." With the hashes and salts in hand, attackers can make password guesses using their own hardware until they potentially recover the original credentials. Whether those attempts succeed depends on the strength of each password and the hashing algorithm Fishbrain used, which the company did not disclose. Fishbrain did not comment on the scale of the breach or how many of its claimed 20 million-plus users were affected. The Register asked Fishbrain for more information. After discovering the intrusion and conducting an initial forensic investigation, Fishbrain patched the vulnerability and reset every user's password. Customers must create a new one the next time they log in. Fishbrain also said it "restricted access to the affected environment," strengthened its security controls, and initiated "a broader review of our data security measures" while the investigation continues. Fisherfolk should also keep an eye out for phisherfolk using the stolen personal data to bait follow-on attacks. ®

entries.title:
So happy to finally share the news in person

It’s been a wild ride for Hugging Face. We certainly d...
entries.content:
So happy to finally share the news in person  
  
It’s been a wild ride for Hugging Face. We certainly did not anticipate, back in 2016, as a tiny team of scrappy underdogs, that the field would grow so much or that the impact we could have on it would become so massive.  
  
I remember [@julien\_c](https://x.com/julien_c) joking that « code will be a subset of ML » several years ago. The joke turned out to be true, and the pleasure we’ve had being part of this transformation and pushing an alternative vision of AI as open, collaborative and distributed has been and still is immense.  
  
We’ve always built things seriously while not taking ourselves too seriously at Hugging Face (special congrats if you find the Hugging Face and Nvidia references hidden in our $12,930,300,000 acquisition price), and we plan to keep doing what we've been doing, just at a much bigger scale, backed by the resources, expertise and drive of Nvidia. And to be clear, nothing changes for our users today.  
  
No company in the world has been a more natural fit with our mission than Nvidia. From open-source, open-weights and open science to robotics and AI for science, they have been close partners across everything we care about. So when Jensen offered [@ClementDelangue](https://x.com/ClementDelangue) the opportunity to double down on building the Hub as an open, independent and compute agnostic platform, we decided the time was right to start the next 10 years of our journey together.  
  
We’re at an important inflection point for open-source AI, where scale and compute are becoming increasingly essential. We’re excited to have the resources to push further, build more ambitiously, and bring you even more projects and news in the coming months.
